_comment: Generated by visuals/tools/build-descriptors.py from the code (gfx-bench manifest, plugin.rs), faces.json, groups.json and each crate's parameter tables. Do not edit.

polarity.name: Polarity
polarity.help: Fixes a phase problem between two lanes

presets.name: Solo lift +4 dB
presets.desc: Flat +4 dB after the amp: the solo gets louder without changing its tone
presets.notes: Place after the amp (or cab): no change in saturation, only level. Click-free on a footswitch

presets.name: Amp push +8 dB
presets.desc: Flat +8 dB before the amp: more breakup and sustain from an amp that is already crunchy
presets.notes: Before the amp it is a gain change, not a level change: the amp's own voice gets hotter

presets.name: Hot front end +12 dB
presets.desc: The full +12 dB before the amp: turns a clean amp's edge into crunch, or a crunch into a lead
presets.notes: Flat boost: unlike a tight boost it also pushes the lows; for high-gain amps use gfx-shem instead

presets.name: Unity volume
presets.desc: 0 dB, bit-transparent: the volume-pedal block at rest, ready for an EXP pedal
presets.notes: Exactly 1.0 at 0 dB. Map EXP on gain (−60 → 0 dB) for swells or a volume pedal

presets.name: Rhythm level −4 dB
presets.desc: Lowers the part by 4 dB: sits a rhythm scene under the lead or matches two lanes
presets.notes: Level-matching tool; exact dB, smoothed so a scene change never clicks

presets.name: Polarity flip
presets.desc: Unity gain with the polarity inverted: fixes cancellation between two lanes or two mics
presets.notes: Use when a blended lane thins the low end; the 5 ms crossfade makes it switchable live

thresh.name: Threshold
thresh.help: Opening level, peak, after the sidechain filters

hold.name: Hold
hold.help: Stays open this long after the envelope falls below the close threshold

release.name: Release
release.help: Time from open to range, linear in dB

lpf.name: Sidechain High Cut
lpf.help: Butterworth low-pass on detection; ≥ 20 kHz = off

follow.name: Follow Decay
follow.help: Release adapts to how the note ended (0.25× – 4×)

damp.name: Tail Damp
damp.help: Highs close before the level (hiss under decaying notes)

hum.name: Hum Filter
hum.help: Notches mains hum out of detection

listen.name: Listen
listen.help: Outputs the filtered sidechain, for setting hpf / lpf / hum

presets.name: Pedalboard standard
presets.desc: Hard gate just above the guitar's idle noise: open in 1 ms, closes after a short hold with a 150 ms fade
presets.notes: golem's Standard gate kept; −3 dB hysteresis stops chatter on decaying notes without holding the noise open

presets.name: Soft fade gate
presets.desc: Low threshold and a slow 400 ms fade with follow decay: hiss goes away, ringing chords are never cut
presets.notes: Follow decay stretches the release up to 4× on natural decays, so sustained crunch chords fade like an amp turned down

presets.name: Tight chugs before the amp
presets.desc: Fast gate before a high-gain amp; 120 Hz sidechain low cut makes palm-mute stops snap shut in ~10 ms

refs.why: staccato riffs with dead-silent stops between mutes, gate set for it
refs.source: Reverb.com, Misha Mansoor outlines the ultimate metal pedalboard (undated)

presets.notes: golem's Chug-tight from the design doc. hpf 120 Hz shrinks the close window to 10 ms (tighter, not just less sensitive); follow keeps held chords

presets.name: Amp-hiss gate keyed from the DI
presets.desc: Gate after the amp listening to the clean DI: amp hiss is cut on the guitar's own timing, at any gain
presets.notes: Needs golem to route the lane DI into the key bus; without it the gate falls back to the main input and the threshold is then too low

presets.name: Breakdown stop-start
presets.desc: Very fast hard gate for stop-start breakdowns: 25 ms release, high sidechain cut, no follow, silence on every rest
presets.notes: Follow off on purpose: every stop is a hard stop. Too aggressive for sustained chords, use chug-tight there

presets.name: High-gain lead expander
presets.desc: 3:1 soft-knee expander with tail damp: hiss fades first under a long lead note, the note's end is never chopped
presets.notes: From the doc's lead row. Expansion instead of switching keeps vibrato tails alive; damp 60 % takes 7 dB from the highs before the level moves

presets.name: Single-coil hum guard
presets.desc: Notches 50 Hz mains hum out of detection so the gate can sit 6 dB lower; gentle range keeps the playing natural
presets.notes: Set hum to 60 Hz in the Americas. Range −40 dB rather than silence: a strat's buzz is lowered, never pumping

presets.name: Natural clean expander
presets.desc: 2:1 expander floored at −20 dB: lowers noise between clean funk stabs without ever fully closing
presets.notes: The doc's clean / funk row. Gentle enough for ghost notes and muted scratches to stay audible

presets.name: Doom sustain gate
presets.desc: Low threshold, long hold and an 800 ms decay-following fade: huge sustained chords ring, silence after they die
presets.notes: Slow riffs leave long rests: follow decay lets a held chord fade on its own, damp removes the fizz first

presets.name: Bass gate
presets.desc: Bass gate with a 40 ms close window (no chatter on a low B), 50 ms hold and a 250 ms fade
presets.notes: golem's Bass gate from the doc. 5 ms attack keeps the low fundamental's first cycle clean; lpf 8 kHz ignores string noise

presets.name: Down-tuned bass, tight
presets.desc: Faster bass gate that stops with the guitars' chugs; low-pass detection ignores pick clank and fret noise
presets.notes: Pair with chug-tight on the guitars so bass and guitars stop together

presets.name: Live mic bleed reducer
presets.desc: Lowers stage bleed in a vocal mic by 15 dB between phrases; long hold and release never clip a word's tail
presets.notes: golem's Vocal gate from the doc. Range −15 dB reduces bleed without the pumping ambience of a full close

presets.name: Tom mic gate
presets.desc: Opens on tom hits, ignores cymbals through a 6 kHz detection cut; natural decay, bleed lowered by 40 dB
presets.notes: Hysteresis −6 dB plus follow lets the drum's ring decay; detection band 60 Hz – 6 kHz rejects kick rumble and cymbal wash

presets.name: 80s gated drum room
presets.desc: Hard gate on a crushed room mic or reverb: full ambience for a quarter second, then a sudden 40 ms cut

refs.why: heavily compressed room mic gated to cut the big ambience short
Padgham found the gated room sound on Gabriel's third album at Townhouse

presets.notes: Put a heavy compressor before it on the room or reverb return. The effect is the abrupt all-to-nothing cut: hold sets the size, keep release short

thresh.name: Threshold
thresh.help: Level above which the compressor starts to reduce gain

ratio.name: Ratio
ratio.help: How much the level above the threshold is reduced (30:1 ≈ limiting)

attack.name: Attack
attack.help: How fast gain reduction sets in once the level exceeds the threshold

release.name: Release
release.help: With auto_release: the fast stage, the slow one follows

character.name: Character
character.help: The compressor's voicing: clean, bus glue, FET, opto or pedal

knee.name: Knee
knee.help: Quadratic soft knee in dB, the same in every character

mix.name: Mix
mix.help: Parallel compression; the dry runs through the same oversampling path when it is active, so the blend never combs

link.name: Stereo Link
link.help: Stereo layout: 100 = one gain for both channels

presets.name: Even clean guitar
presets.desc: Transparent 4:1 with a 6 dB knee and dual-path release: strums sit at one level, no pumping between them
presets.notes: The doc's clean-guitar row, golem's Standard

presets.name: Chicken-picking squash
presets.desc: OTA pedal squash, 8:1 with a 3 ms attack: snappy pick click on top, every note of a hybrid-picked run equal

refs.why: Nashville session lines played through a compressor pedal

presets.notes: The doc's funk / country row. Before the amp, into a clean Fender-type voice

presets.name: Squash with the pick kept
presets.desc: Same pedal squash blended 60 % with the dry: sustain from the wet, the natural pick attack from the dry
presets.notes: The doc's parallel row; the blend-knob pedals' trick. Coherent mix means no comb at 60 %

presets.name: Funk chop, compressed clean
presets.desc: FET 4:1, 8 ms attack, fast release, 80 % wet: tight 16th-note scratches that pop out evenly without losing snap

refs.why: bright, even, mostly direct funk rhythm guitar

presets.notes: Accounts of Rodgers' chain disagree on compression; this is the sound in its spirit, not a documented setting

presets.name: Singing lead sustain
presets.desc: Pedal-style compressor before a fuzz or drive: long notes hold and bloom, a hot front end for endless sustain

refs.why: Gilmour's compressor pedal into a fuzz for the solo's sustain
refs.source: Guitar World feature, reprinted in Australian Guitar, 2021

presets.notes: Long release so the gain rises slowly as the note decays: sustain without an audible swell

presets.name: Drop-tuned rhythm control
presets.desc: Clean 3:1 with a 150 Hz sidechain low cut: evens out low-tuned riffs without the low strings pumping the mix
presets.notes: After the amp and cab. High-gain is already compressed: this only catches the open-string peaks

presets.name: Acoustic strum leveller
presets.desc: Gentle opto 3:1 with an 80 Hz sidechain cut: a piezo or mic'd acoustic stays even, body thumps don't duck it
presets.notes: Slow-ish opto keeps the strum's attack; the sidechain cut stops a palm slap from pulling the whole level down

presets.name: Glue after amp and cab
presets.desc: Bus 2.5:1, 30 ms attack, 250 ms release: 2 – 3 dB of glue after the cab, transients kept
presets.notes: The doc's glue row

presets.name: Fingerstyle bass, smooth opto
presets.desc: Opto 4:1, slow attack, two-stage release: fingerstyle notes even out, warm and unobtrusive

refs.why: mixer Mick Guzauski picks a slow LA-2A for smooth vocals and bass
refs.source: Universal Audio blog, 10 Questions with Mick Guzauski (undated)

presets.notes: Opto's release lengthens after long reduction, so a held note never swells back up audibly

presets.name: Anchored rock bass
presets.desc: FET 6:1, 35 ms attack, 120 Hz sidechain low cut: pick attack through, sustain locked, the low E doesn't pump
presets.notes: golem's Bass anchor from the doc's bass row; drive 20 % adds the FET's odd harmonics for small-speaker audibility

presets.name: Slap and pop control
presets.desc: Fast feed-forward 8:1 with a 1 ms attack: thumb slaps and pops tamed so the ghost notes come up

refs.why: slap pioneer whose rack held a fast dbx 160X compressor

presets.notes: Clean = feed-forward like a VCA; the full-band detector is wanted here, pops are what must trigger it

presets.name: Smooth vocal leveller
presets.desc: Opto 3:1, 25 ms attack, two-stage release: a lead vocal levelled without audible grab, warm and forward

refs.why: mixer Carlos de la Garza starts every vocal on a Gray LA-2A
refs.source: Universal Audio blog, Carlos de la Garza interview (undated)

presets.notes: The doc's voice row, golem's Vocal opto; sidechain cut keeps plosives and stage rumble from pumping it

presets.name: Upfront rock vocal
presets.desc: FET 6:1, 2 ms attack, fast release with a little drive: a shouted vocal pinned in front of loud guitars
presets.notes: FET shortens its times further on short peaks: every syllable stays at the front in a dense mix

presets.name: Thick parallel vocal
presets.desc: FET squeezed 7 – 10 dB and blended about 30 % under the dry vocal: thickness and punch, the dynamics stay

refs.why: Chiccarelli tucked a heavily squeezed parallel 1176 under the lead vocal
refs.source: Vintage King, Five Sounds with Joe Chiccarelli, 2022

presets.notes: Slow-to-mid attack, fast-to-mid release as in the interview; mix 30 % stands for the parallel bus fader

presets.name: Drum bus glue
presets.desc: Bus 4:1, 30 ms attack, auto release: 2 – 4 dB on the kit, hits keep their crack, the kit sounds as one
presets.notes: Bus-console style settings; sidechain cut so the kick alone doesn't duck the cymbals

presets.name: Crushed parallel drums
presets.desc: FET 10:1 crushing the kit, blended 35 % with the dry: sustain and room come up, the transients stay dry
presets.notes: New York-style parallel compression in one block; the coherent mix means no comb when blending

presets.name: Keys glue
presets.desc: Bus 2:1, slow attack and release: keys and pads gently held together, playing dynamics intact
presets.notes: golem's Keys glue

presets.name: Gentle leveller, capped
presets.desc: Clean 2:1 with a wide knee and reduction capped at 6 dB: evens any source, can never squash it
presets.notes: The doc's range row, golem's Gentle

threshold.name: Threshold
threshold.help: Maximum output sample level, no makeup

release.name: Release
release.help: With auto_release: scales the adaptive release

gain.name: Input Gain
gain.help: Drive into the limiter (x42's hidden input gain)

style.name: Style
style.help: How peaks are held: clean, punchy (faster release) or clip (soft clipping)

clip.name: Clip Softness
clip.help: 0 = hard (ADAA); 100 = soft from 6 dB under the threshold

presets.name: End-of-lane safety
presets.desc: Inaudible zero-latency ceiling at −3 dBFS: untouched below it, catches only the odd runaway peak
presets.notes: The doc's safety row. threshold is the ceiling with no makeup: what you set is the peak you get

presets.name: In-ear and monitor guard
presets.desc: Clean limiter at −6 dBFS with a calm release on a monitor send: feedback squeals and dropped mics cannot spike the ears
presets.notes: Zero latency matters on in-ears (comb with bone conduction); a soft clip handles the first cycle of a sudden spike

presets.name: Louder lead, PA-safe
presets.desc: +6 dB into a punchy limiter at −3 dBFS: the solo jumps forward, pick attacks kept, the PA never clips
presets.notes: The doc's louder-lead row; envelope and soft clip share the work

presets.name: Loud and clipped
presets.desc: Pure alias-free soft clipping driven +9 dB: a dense, saturated wall for loud live leads and synths
presets.notes: The doc's loud row. Clip style lands up to 1.7 dB under the threshold (down-sampler headroom)

presets.name: Bass peaks, no low-E distortion
presets.desc: Clean limiter with a slow release and LF hold at −4 dBFS: slaps and low notes held without riding the waveform
presets.notes: The doc's bass row: auto release holds over one LF period, so the gain never tracks a 41 Hz cycle

presets.name: Vocal peak ceiling
presets.desc: Clean limiter at −4 dBFS with a 120 ms release after the vocal compressor: screams and plosives held

refs.why: FOH Brian Pomp ends the lead vocal chain on a limiter
refs.source: Vintage King, Brian Pomp FOH interview, 2017

presets.notes: The doc's vocal row. A stage singer's peaks overshoot any compressor's attack: this is the last word

presets.name: Backing tracks, transparent
presets.desc: 2 ms lookahead, true-peak ceiling at −1 dBTP: playback and keys limited with no first-cycle shaping at all
presets.notes: Reports 2 ms of latency: fine for tracks and pads, avoid on a played instrument monitored in ears

lowcut.name: Low Cut
lowcut.help: High-pass filter: removes the lows below this frequency

midgain.name: Mid Gain
midgain.help: Boost or cut of the mid bell

midfreq.name: Mid Freq
midfreq.help: Bell frequency (an EXP sweep = a fixed wah)

midprop.name: Proportional Q
midprop.help: 0 = constant Q; 100 = API-like narrowing with gain

mid2gain.name: Mid 2 Gain
mid2gain.help: Second bell: a guitarist's commonest move is two at once (cut the mud, lift the presence)

mid2freq.name: Mid 2 Freq
mid2freq.help: Centre frequency of the second mid band

mid2q.name: Mid 2 Q
mid2q.help: Same proportional-Q amount as the first bell

highfreq.name: High Freq
highfreq.help: High shelf corner (ReaEQ's band 4 value to read on the bench)

airfreq.name: Air Freq
airfreq.help: Corner frequency of the air shelf

highcut.name: High Cut
highcut.help: Low-pass, 12 dB / oct, matched (no forced zero at Nyquist)

harsh_freq.name: De-harsh Freq
harsh_freq.help: Centre of the band the de-harsher watches and tames

harsh_thresh.name: De-harsh Threshold
harsh_thresh.help: Band level relative to the full band

harsh_range.name: De-harsh Range
harsh_range.help: Maximum cut the de-harsher may apply

presets.name: Standard
presets.desc: Flat EQ with an 80 Hz high-pass: removes rumble and handling noise, changes nothing else
presets.notes: golem's Standard preset kept as is: the neutral starting point a hand-placed EQ gets

presets.name: Post-cab guitar cleanup
presets.desc: High-pass 90 Hz, steep low-pass 7 kHz, -3 dB at 350 Hz and a de-harsher: a cab sim sitting in a band mix
presets.notes: The two cuts every mixed guitar gets: lows go to the bass and kick, the fizz above 7 kHz is cab-sim air no mic hears

presets.name: Light guitar polish
presets.desc: High-pass 90 Hz, gentle 2 dB dip at 800 Hz, a touch of high shelf: a cleaner, slightly more open guitar
presets.notes: golem's Guitar polish kept as is

presets.name: Mid scoop
presets.desc: 5 dB cut at 550 Hz with a 2 dB high shelf: a hollower, wider-sounding crunch rhythm
presets.notes: golem's Mid scoop kept as is; proportional Q narrows the cut as it deepens, so the 1 kHz bite survives

presets.name: Deep V metal rhythm
presets.desc: Deep 7 dB cut at 750 Hz, lift at 90 Hz and 6 kHz, steep 9 kHz low-pass: the classic scooped thrash rhythm

refs.why: Mark IIC+ five-band graphic EQ set in a V, deepest cut near 750 Hz

presets.notes: Graphic-EQ V moved to bells; keeps 2.2 kHz pick attack so the scoop does not vanish in the band. Great alone, thin in a dense mix

presets.name: Tight mid push into the amp
presets.desc: Steep 140 Hz high-pass and +5 dB at 720 Hz, highs eased: tightens a high-gain amp's palm mutes from the front

refs.why: Misha Mansoor tightens his high-gain amps with an overdrive in front

presets.notes: Placed BEFORE the amp: an overdrive-pedal curve without the clipping. Less bass into the preamp = less flub; +3 dB out hits the input harder

presets.name: High-gain fizz tamer
presets.desc: Dynamic cut around 3.5 kHz plus a steep 8.5 kHz low-pass: removes fizz on sustained chords, keeps mute attack
presets.notes: The de-harsher is relative to the full band, so it reacts to fizz, not to loudness; the static 5.5 kHz dip handles cab-sim sizzle

presets.name: Solo mid lift
presets.desc: +4 dB broad bell at 1.2 kHz and +2 dB output: the lead steps forward of the band without more gain
presets.notes: Mids carry a guitar through a mix far better than volume or treble; put it on the solo scene, after the amp

presets.name: Parked wah lead
presets.desc: Narrow +12 dB resonant peak at 900 Hz, lows trimmed: a wah left half-open, nasal and vocal (EXP on Mid Freq)

refs.why: leads through a wah parked at one spot instead of rocked
half-open wah colouring his Ziggy-era lead tone

presets.notes: Constant Q (midprop 0) keeps the peak narrow; -5 dB output offsets the peak's added level. Assign EXP to midfreq to sweep it

presets.name: Bass clean-up
presets.desc: 35 Hz high-pass, 2 dB dip at 700 Hz, a hint of top: a cleaner bass DI that leaves room for the kick
presets.notes: golem's Bass clean-up kept as is

presets.name: Scooped slap bass
presets.desc: Low shelf +3 dB at 80 Hz, -5 dB at 500 Hz, bright shelf and air: thumb thump and pop with the mids out

refs.why: both-pickup Jazz bass slap with the mids scooped and the top open
Flea's bright, percussive slap lines

presets.notes: The smile curve slap players dial; the de-harsher at 5 kHz catches the loudest pops so the bright shelf can stay up

presets.name: Vintage flatwound thump
presets.desc: Warm lift at 100 Hz, +2 dB at 700 Hz, highs rolled off from 4 kHz: an old P-bass with flats and tone down

refs.why: flatwound Precision with the tone rolled back on Motown sessions

presets.notes: The 700 Hz bump is the note definition that a P-bass keeps in a mix even when its top is gone

presets.name: Metal bass clank
presets.desc: Tight low end, -3 dB at 400 Hz, +5 dB at 2.2 kHz: a pick-attack clank that cuts through high-gain guitars
presets.notes: Low mids are the guitars' space; the bass is heard as sub plus upper-mid clank. Use after a bass drive or on the DI branch

presets.name: Acoustic stage anti-feedback
presets.desc: Steep 90 Hz high-pass, narrow -6 dB notch at 120 Hz, -3.5 dB piezo quack at 1.2 kHz, air: a piezo acoustic on stage
presets.notes: Body boom near 100-120 Hz is the first to feed back; sweep midfreq to the room's howl. The quack band varies (1-3 kHz) per pickup

presets.name: Vocal clarity
presets.desc: 120 Hz high-pass, -2.5 dB of box at 400 Hz, +2.5 dB high shelf: a clearer, less muddy live vocal
presets.notes: golem's Vocal clarity kept as is

presets.name: Airy live vocal
presets.desc: 100 Hz high-pass, -2.5 dB at 400 Hz, +3 dB air shelf at 12 kHz, de-ess around 6 kHz: open but never sharp
presets.notes: Presence comes from the air shelf, not 3-5 kHz, so stage monitors feed back less; the dynamic band acts as a de-esser

presets.name: Telephone band-pass
presets.desc: Steep high-pass 350 Hz and low-pass 3.4 kHz, +4 dB honk at 1.5 kHz: a voice through a phone or a tiny amp

refs.why: vocals sung through a small practice amp for a lo-fi, band-limited voice

presets.notes: 300 Hz-3.4 kHz is the phone line's band; the +4 dB output makes up most of the level the filters remove. Also works on drum loops

presets.name: Keys out of the bass's way
presets.desc: 120 Hz high-pass, -2 dB at 300 Hz, light lift at 2.5 kHz: piano or pad that sits above the bass and guitars
presets.notes: A full-range piano left hand fights the bass; raise lowcut to 200 Hz in a dense band, lower it for solo piano

presets.name: Dusty lo-fi keys
presets.desc: 90 Hz high-pass, warm lift at 150 Hz, steep 4.5 kHz low-pass and a dark tilt: keys that sound sampled from vinyl
presets.notes: Pair with a bitcrusher or tape wobble for the full effect; auto gain keeps it as loud as the bypassed keys

presets.name: Dark archtop warmth
presets.desc: -3 dB tilt around 1 kHz, gentle 6 kHz low-pass, loudness held by auto gain: a round, woody clean guitar
presets.notes: The tone-knob-at-3 sound without the volume drop; auto gain is static, so nothing pumps

presets.name: Boost-and-cut low end
presets.desc: +4 dB low shelf at 60 Hz with a broad -2 dB dip at 200 Hz: deeper thump, less box, for kick, bass or drum loops
presets.notes: The passive-console trick of boosting and cutting next to each other; the 25 Hz high-pass stops the shelf from feeding subsonic energy

thresh.name: Threshold
thresh.help: Relative: band − full band; Absolute: band level

freq.name: Frequency
freq.help: Start of the detection band; corner of the shelf / centre of the bell

listen.name: Listen
listen.help: Solo of what the detector hears

detect.name: Detection
detect.help: Absolute = the JSFX's behaviour, the default so golem presets keep their meaning (rack session's advice); Relative = level-independent

shape.name: Shape
shape.help: How the sibilance is cut: high shelf, narrow bell or wide band

focus.name: Focus
focus.help: Vocal adds the zero-crossing confidence weight; Allround = pure high-frequency limiter (guitar de-harsh, cymbals)

ratio.name: Ratio
ratio.help: The JSFX's fixed ratio, now a parameter

presets.name: Live lead vocal
presets.desc: Level-independent de-essing from 6 kHz, shelf cut up to 8 dB: holds when the singer backs off or a comp sits upstream

refs.why: FOH Brian Pomp puts a de-esser in the live lead vocal chain
refs.source: Vintage King, Brian Pomp FOH interview, 2017

presets.notes: The doc's live-lead row. Relative detection matters live: mic distance changes all night

presets.name: Bright high voice
presets.desc: Narrow bell at 7.5 kHz: a high, bright voice's sharp 's' notched out while the air above stays
presets.notes: The doc's bright-female row

presets.name: Low voice, lower sibilance
presets.desc: Detection from 4.5 kHz with a shelf: a deep voice's duller, lower 's' and 'sh' caught without lisping
presets.notes: Vocal focus's zero-crossing weight keeps bright vowels from triggering this lower band

presets.name: Heavy sibilance, wide band
presets.desc: 10:1 wide-band reduction up to 12 dB: a very sibilant singer or a bright condenser mic tamed hard
presets.notes: The doc's heavy row with Wide, which ducks the whole voice briefly: the cleanest-sounding way on a solo vocal

presets.name: Close-mic rap and speech
presets.desc: 5.5 kHz shelf, 8:1, fast 40 ms release: dense, close-mic'd rap or speech de-essed word by word
presets.notes: Fast delivery leaves no gap between esses: the short release keeps the next vowel from being dulled

presets.name: Transparent with lookahead
presets.desc: 5 ms lookahead catches the very start of each 's': fully transparent de-essing for playback or recording
presets.notes: Reports 5 ms of latency: not for a singer monitoring themselves in ears

presets.name: Overdrive fizz tamer
presets.desc: Allround high-frequency limiter, bell at 3.5 kHz: pick click and fizz of a driven guitar softened only when they spike
presets.notes: The doc's de-harsh row. After amp and cab: a static EQ cut would dull the palm mutes too

presets.name: Cymbal and hi-hat tamer
presets.desc: Allround shelf from 8 kHz: harsh crashes and hats on overheads or a drum bus pulled down only when they ring
presets.notes: Allround: no zero-crossing weight, cymbals are noise-like and must be treated as a whole

model.name: Model
model.help: The wah circuit whose sweep, Q and voicing are played

mix.name: Mix
mix.help: Wet level against the dry signal (100 % = wah only)

mode.name: Mode
mode.help: Manual = the pedal sweeps; auto = the envelope sweeps; alien = both

taper.name: Taper
taper.help: How the pedal travel maps onto the sweep; Model = the circuit's own pot

toe.name: Toe
toe.help: Where the sweep ends at toe down (percent of the full range)

auto_engage.name: Auto Engage
auto_engage.help: Switches the wah on when the pedal moves, off when it rests at heel

engage_wait.name: Engage Wait
engage_wait.help: How long the pedal must rest at heel before the wah switches off

env_sens.name: Envelope Sensitivity
env_sens.help: How strongly playing dynamics move the sweep (auto and alien modes)

env_att.name: Envelope Attack
env_att.help: How fast the envelope follows a louder note

env_rel.name: Envelope Release
env_rel.help: How fast the envelope falls back after the note

presets.name: Classic rock pedal wah
presets.desc: The standard Cry Baby voice on the expression pedal: vocal heel-to-toe sweep for rock leads

refs.why: Slash's stock Cry Baby on the Appetite-era solos

presets.notes: golem's wah block voice (GCB-95, 408 Hz to 2.25 kHz); a little resonance clipping for realism; EXP on wah

presets.name: High-gain lead wah
presets.desc: Cry Baby before a high-gain amp, slightly lower Q and a level push: screaming, cutting metal leads

refs.why: Hammett's Cry Baby lead break cutting over the riff
signature Cry Baby wah in his Black Label Society rig

presets.notes: The crate's high-gain start: Q 80 tames fizz into the amp, +3 dB hits the preamp harder; auto-engage so the foot only rocks

presets.name: Dark, wide grunge wah
presets.desc: Cry Baby with a wider sweep and a toe stop short of the top: dark, squashed wah on heavy riffs

refs.why: Cantrell's dark, punchy wah woven through the riffs

presets.notes: Range 120 widens the sweep downward; toe 85 keeps the top dark (the idea of a toe-trim pot)

presets.name: Parked-wah honk
presets.desc: Wah parked just past the middle: a fixed, nasal mid-boost that makes a driven amp snarl

refs.why: Mick Ronson's parked wah for a honking, aggressive lead tone
Brian May's wah used in fixed positions as a tone filter
Knopfler's riff through a partly-open, fixed wah

presets.notes: No EXP needed: the crate's parked-wah use (0.4 to 0.6); move wah to taste for more nasal (lower) or more cutting (higher)

presets.name: Boosted solo wah
presets.desc: Cry Baby with extra Q and a solo-level boost: the wah also lifts the lead over the band
presets.notes: Volume +5 dB covers a 535Q-style boost: engaging the wah (auto-engage) is also the solo boost

presets.name: Switchless short-throw wah
presets.desc: Turns on when the pedal moves, off when parked at heel; shorter travel with an S taper
presets.notes: Crate's switchless and smaller-travel uses together: heel 10 / toe 85 avoid the extreme mud and shriek

presets.name: Late-60s British wah
presets.desc: The original Italian-style wah voice: smooth, vocal sweep for psychedelic blues leads

refs.why: Clapton named a Vox wah for the song's wah parts
the scratched, muted wah intro and wah-soaked leads

presets.notes: Vox V847 with its own linear pot law (heel = low, fixed in this crate); drive 25 lets the peak clip into a fuzz

presets.name: Funk wacka rhythm
presets.desc: Narrow, peaky wah for muted 16th-note scratching: the 'wacka-wacka' chika rhythm

refs.why: Skip Pitts' rhythmic wah-wah guitar intro

presets.notes: Crate's funk start: Classic voice with Q 150 makes each rock of the foot a sharp vowel; rock in time with the 16ths

presets.name: Vocal, throaty lead wah
presets.desc: Wide-range, moderately peaky wah voice: a throaty, talking sweep for expressive blues leads
presets.notes: Clyde voicing (369 Hz to 2.37 kHz, Q 4.17 per Fractal) sweeps wider than the Cry Baby: more 'vowel' per inch

presets.name: Fuzzy British wah
presets.desc: Sharp, aggressive vintage wah voice driven into clipping: snarling fuzz-wah for psych and stoner
presets.notes: Colorsound keeps its inverted log pot law; drive 45 clips the resonance into a fuzz of its own

presets.name: Sixties beat-group wah
presets.desc: Gentle, lower-Q vintage British wah voice: a soft, round sweep for crunchy 60s rhythm
presets.notes: Selmer voicing with its linear pot law; Q 90 softens it further

presets.name: Bass wah, lows kept
presets.desc: Bass-voiced wah blended with the dry: a talking sweep on the mids while the low end stays put

refs.why: Cliff Burton's distorted bass solo through a wah

presets.notes: Crate's bass start: Bass 105Q voicing with mix 70 so the fundamental never disappears

presets.name: Hands-free envelope wah
presets.desc: The wah voice swept by picking dynamics instead of the foot: quacks on each attack
presets.notes: Crate's auto-wah-without-a-pedal use; for a dedicated envelope filter prefer gfx-autowah

presets.name: Rhythmic LFO wah sweep
presets.desc: An LFO rocks the wah on its own at about two sweeps a second: a cycling, psychedelic wah
presets.notes: freq is the alien LFO in BPM (120 = 2 Hz), free-running, not host-synced: set it near the song tempo

presets.name: Keys funk pedal wah
presets.desc: Round, mid-focused wah on clavinet or electric piano, swept by the foot for funky comping
presets.notes: No drive on keys; mix 85 keeps a little dry so low notes of the clav stay full

wah.name: Sensitivity
wah.help: Envelope window: higher = reacts to softer playing

type.name: Type
type.help: Default Wah: golem's autowah block played GxAutoWah, an envelope-driven Cry Baby; presets keep that sound

poles.name: Poles
poles.help: Filter slope: 2 poles = vocal, 4 poles = deeper, synth-like

direction.name: Direction
direction.help: Up = louder notes sweep upward; Down = they sweep downward

peak.name: Peak
peak.help: Resonance of the filter: higher = a sharper, more vocal peak

attack.name: Attack
attack.help: How fast the sweep follows a picked note

release.name: Release
release.help: How fast the sweep falls back after the note

mix.name: Mix
mix.help: Wet level against the dry signal (100 % = filter only)

level.name: Level
level.help: Check plain ↔ normalized on REAPER (negative minimum)

source.name: Source
source.help: What moves the filter: playing dynamics, an LFO, sample and hold, or both

rate.name: Rate
rate.help: Speed of the LFO or sample-and-hold source

sync.name: Sync
sync.help: Locks the LFO to the host tempo; Off = the Rate control

presets.name: Envelope Cry Baby
presets.desc: A Cry Baby resonance swept by picking dynamics: each attack opens the wah, the decay closes it
presets.notes: Keeps golem's autowah block sound (GxAutoWah, Wah type); sensitivity a touch above default for typical DI levels

presets.name: Clavinet funk quack
presets.desc: Opto band-pass envelope filter on clavinet: every keystroke quacks upward, fast and percussive

refs.why: his Clavinet riff played through a Mu-Tron III

presets.notes: Crate's keys/clav start; Opto mimics the Mu-Tron's LED/LDR lag; +3 dB makes up the band-pass level loss

presets.name: Funk guitar envelope quack
presets.desc: Level-independent band-pass envelope filter: the same quack on muted funk strums at any volume
presets.notes: The crate's Mu-Tron III guitar start: band-pass, up, 250 Hz to 2.5 kHz, peak 5

presets.name: Watery jam-band lead
presets.desc: Band-pass with dry blended in and a lagging opto release: a liquid, vowel-like lead tone

refs.why: Jerry Garcia made the Mu-Tron III part of his lead sound

presets.notes: Crate's Garcia start (BP + dry, opto, release 250 ms): the dry keeps note definition under the vowel

presets.name: Squelchy space bass
presets.desc: Low-pass envelope filter on bass that squelches upward on each note while the sub stays dry

refs.why: used the Mu-Tron III on his bass with Parliament/Funkadelic

presets.notes: The crate's Bootsy start; bass keep 120 Hz (Linkwitz-Riley) keeps the bottom from thinning when the filter closes

presets.name: Synth-like 4-pole bass
presets.desc: Steep, resonant 4-pole low-pass opened by each note: bass that sounds like an analog mono synth
presets.notes: Crate's Moog-style start: 4 poles + peak 10 give the synth 'zap'; fast attack for slap and pick

presets.name: Downward 'ow' sweep
presets.desc: Envelope sweeps down on loud notes: each attack starts bright and falls into an 'ow'
presets.notes: Direction Down mirrors the sweep (Mu-Tron drive down switch)

presets.name: Chewy saturated filter
presets.desc: Signal pushed into a resonant band-pass: a thick, chewy, slightly growling envelope quack
presets.notes: Crate's chewy start (drive 12 dB, peak 8): saturation inside the filter, as when a Q-Tron is driven hard

presets.name: Talking vowel lead
presets.desc: Formant filter morphing a-e-i-o-u with picking strength: a talk-box-like vocal lead

refs.why: talk-box vowels that this formant filter imitates

presets.notes: Crate's talk-box start (Vowel, up, sensitivity 0.6); slower attack lets the vowel 'speak' rather than click

presets.name: Tempo-synced filter sweep
presets.desc: An LFO locked to quarter notes sweeps a resonant 4-pole low-pass: a pulsing synth-style filter
presets.notes: Crate's tempo-synced use; the LFO ignores playing dynamics, so it works on pads, loops and chords alike

presets.name: Random stepped filter
presets.desc: Sample-and-hold jumps the band-pass to a new random frequency every sixteenth note
presets.notes: Crate's random-stepped use: the classic synth S&H 'computer' burble, synced to the host

presets.name: Offbeat skank chirp
presets.desc: Fast high-pass envelope filter on offbeat chops: a thin, chirpy attack that stays out of the bass
presets.notes: High-pass sweeps up on each chop then relaxes: the skank chirps and leaves the low mids to the bass

presets.name: Breathing envelope wobble
presets.desc: Playing dynamics plus a slow LFO move the filter together: notes quack and then keep swaying
presets.notes: On electric piano: the LFO at 0.4 Hz keeps sustained chords moving after the envelope settles

rate.name: Rate
rate.help: Speed of the volume modulation (when Sync is Off)

depth.name: Depth
depth.help: Trough gain = 1 − depth; lamp drive in Optical / Neon

model.name: Model
model.help: The tremolo circuit: clean VCA, valve bias, optical cell, neon or harmonic (two bands in opposition)

sync.name: Sync
sync.help: Locks the rate to the host tempo; Off = the Rate control

xover.name: Crossover
xover.help: Split frequency of the Harmonic model's two bands

level.name: Level
level.help: Makeup (a tremolo lowers the average level)

presets.name: Optical amp throb
presets.desc: Medium-speed photocell tremolo: rounded, lopsided dips like a 60s combo amp's built-in effect
presets.notes: Lamp + LDR shapes the sine into long highs and short dips; depth 0.6 throbs without chopping; +1.5 dB makes up the average drop

presets.name: Jungle-beat pulse
presets.desc: Deep, fast, choppy tremolo that cuts chords in and out over a clave strum

refs.why: the DeArmond trem's uneven warble trailing his clave rhythm

presets.notes: Neon strike/extinguish gives the choppy, near-gated dips at full depth; 6.5 Hz sits around the beat's subdivisions without syncing

presets.name: Swampy bias breathe
presets.desc: Slow-ish valve-bias tremolo that adds grit at the trough and softens when you dig in

refs.why: the swampy amp vibrato on Fogerty's E7 riff, from his Kustom amp

presets.notes: Bias model: crossover grit near the trough, sag ducks the depth on hard strums; Fogerty calls it vibrato, the Kustom blended both

presets.name: Surf instrumental shimmer
presets.desc: Fast, deep optical tremolo for twangy single-note melodies under spring reverb

refs.why: menacing amp tremolo on sustained twangy chords

presets.notes: The crate's surf starting point (Optical 6 Hz, 0.8); pair with a drippy spring reverb after it

presets.name: Desert western throb
presets.desc: Slower, deep optical pulse for baritone-style twang and reverb-drenched western melodies

refs.why: the twangy, reverb-soaked western guitar this patch evokes

presets.notes: A touch of duck lets the attack of each note ring through before the pulse takes over

presets.name: Synced sixteenth thrum
presets.desc: Deep, choppy amp tremolo locked to sixteenths, slightly offset L/R like several amps at once

refs.why: Marr's rhythm re-amped through several Twins with tremolo on

presets.notes: Neon = blackface choppy; synced so it never drifts (the original had to be edited for that); 60° stereo offset mimics two amp pairs

presets.name: Brownface harmonic pulse
presets.desc: Highs and lows swell in opposition: a phaser-like, level-steady harmonic tremolo
presets.notes: The crate's brownface start: antiphase bands keep the level steady, so little makeup is needed

presets.name: Slow harmonic shimmer
presets.desc: Slow, wide harmonic tremolo that makes sustained chords swirl rather than pulse
presets.notes: Higher crossover moves the swirl into the mids; 90° stereo phase spreads it without becoming an auto-pan

presets.name: Helicopter chop
presets.desc: Full-depth square-wave tremolo at 10 Hz: the signal stutters on and off like rotor blades
presets.notes: golem's old Helicopter; the 2 ms square edges never click; works on clean or high-gain sustained notes

presets.name: Tempo-locked eighth chop
presets.desc: Square tremolo synced to eighth notes, short-on duty: a rhythmic chop for pads and chords
presets.notes: Phase follows the host position, so the chops land on the grid; Clean adds no distortion on synths

presets.name: Pulsing sustain lead
presets.desc: Bias tremolo that backs off while you pick and pulses in on the sustain of each note
presets.notes: Dynamics 0.6 is the crate's 'depth that follows the playing': attacks stay solid, tails throb like a cooking tube amp

presets.name: Slow heavy throb
presets.desc: Slow, deep optical swell on distorted chords: a wall of fuzz that breathes in and out
presets.notes: Place after the drive: a compressed high-gain signal has no dynamics left, so the tremolo must do the pulsing

presets.name: Gentle chord motion
presets.desc: Shallow, slow clean tremolo that adds movement to strummed or arpeggiated chords
presets.notes: The crate's 'subtle movement' start

presets.name: Electric-piano stereo pan
presets.desc: Sine auto-pan between L and R: the stereo vibrato of a suitcase electric piano
presets.notes: 180° = auto-pan: the summed level stays constant, so no makeup; Clean keeps the tines undistorted

presets.name: Clean bass pulse
presets.desc: Tempo-synced clean tremolo on bass: eighth-note pumping without adding grit
presets.notes: Clean model adds no distortion to the fundamental; synced so the pump stays with the drums

presets.name: Warbling psych vocal
presets.desc: Fast, deep tremolo on a voice: the sung line wobbles as if sung through a guitar amp

refs.why: the vocal sung through an amp's tremolo on the outro

presets.notes: Bias with low drive gives the amp's soft compression without audible distortion on the voice

depth.name: Depth
depth.help: 0 – 100 cents (Clean, BBD); stage swing (Varistor, Vibe); V1 → V3 (Scanner)

speed.name: Speed
speed.help: Speed of the pitch modulation (when Sync is Off)

model.name: Model
model.help: The vibrato circuit: clean delay, BBD, varistor, Uni-Vibe-style or organ scanner

shape.name: Shape
shape.help: Random = smoothed, fixed seed, with LFO wobble

tone.name: Tone
tone.help: Low-pass after the vibrato: darker as it rises

sync.name: Sync
sync.help: Locks the speed to the host tempo; Off = the Speed control

level.name: Level
level.help: Output; GxTubeVibrato plays ~6.6 dB louder than unity (golem-rack, pink noise): golem can pin it at insert for preset continuity

presets.name: Gentle pitch wobble
presets.desc: Clean sine vibrato of about 15 cents at 5 Hz, wet only: a light, singing wobble on clean chords
presets.notes: README first application; depth is in cents on Clean (0.15 = 15 cents) and stays the same at any speed

presets.name: Seasick lo-fi warble
presets.desc: Slow, deep, darkened BBD vibrato: a woozy, out-of-tune warble like a stretched cassette

refs.why: Boss VB-2-type wet-only vibrato warble on clean guitar

presets.notes: README 'Seasick'; mix 1 (no dry) is what makes it vibrato rather than chorus

presets.name: Slow detuned glide wash
presets.desc: Very slow, wide BBD pitch drift behind fuzz: chords bend in and out of tune like a held tremolo arm
presets.notes: Random shape at 0.6 Hz bends irregularly instead of cycling, closer to a hand on the bar; place after the fuzz

presets.name: Vintage amp pitch vibrato
presets.desc: Zero-latency phase-modulation vibrato strongest around 1 kHz: the lush true-pitch vibrato of late-50s amps

refs.why: Magnatone amp vibrato (some credit the Bigsby instead)
played a Magnatone Custom 280 with true pitch vibrato

presets.notes: README 'Magnatone amp vibrato'; drive 0.2 adds a little tube colour outside the modulation

presets.name: Vibe-style pitch throb
presets.desc: The vibe's four unequal stages, wet only: a throbbing, liquid pitch vibrato in front of a driven amp

refs.why: Uni-Vibe swirl as the core of his lead sound

presets.notes: README 'Vibe vibrato'; for the vibe's chorus mode use gfx-phaser uni-vibe-throb, or mix 0.5 here

presets.name: Vibrato that grows on held notes
presets.desc: Clean vibrato fading in over 800 ms each time it is engaged: held notes start straight, then sing

refs.why: reportedly moved from a Boss CE-2 to a VB-2 vibrato after Purple Rain

presets.notes: README 'Vibrato that grows' (VB-2 rise time); engage by foot on the note; release ramps only once the bypass hook lands

presets.name: Vibrato-chorus blend
presets.desc: Slow BBD vibrato mixed half and half with the dry: a classic warm chorus built from a pitch vibrato
presets.notes: README 'Chorus from a vibrato'; mix 0.5 is the vibrato/dry blend, stereo 90° spreads the two sides

presets.name: Tonewheel organ deep vibrato
presets.desc: Scanner-type vibrato at its deepest setting, wet only: the shimmering, wavering organ vibrato
presets.notes: Scanner depth 1 = V3 (taps up to 19 of the ladder), speed 6.9 Hz like the rotating capacitor, mix 1 = vibrato

presets.name: Tonewheel organ deep chorus
presets.desc: Scanner vibrato at its deepest blended half with the dry: the thick, animated organ chorus for grooves

refs.why: organ played with the C3 chorus-vibrato setting

presets.notes: Scanner mix 0.5 = the C modes; pair with gfx-rotary on slow or fast for the full organ sound

presets.name: Bass wobble
presets.desc: Moderate BBD vibrato on bass, slightly darkened: a woozy pitch wobble for slow, sparse lines
presets.notes: 20 cents keeps the bass in tune enough to anchor the harmony; there is no bass split here, so the lows move too

presets.name: Lo-fi vocal warble
presets.desc: Light clean pitch vibrato with a random wander on a vocal: a detached, tape-like, slightly unreal voice
presets.notes: 12 cents of random wander reads as tape instability, not as a singer's vibrato; keep it subtle on a lead

presets.name: Tape wow
presets.desc: Slow random pitch drift on any source: the uneven wow of a worn tape machine, for loops and beats
presets.notes: README 'Tape wow'; seeded random LFO so the drift replays the same way each time

presets.name: Tempo-locked quarter warble
presets.desc: Rounded-triangle vibrato locked to quarter notes: the pitch dips in time with the beat on pads or leads
presets.notes: Rounded triangle avoids the square-wave pitch of a plain triangle; speed is ignored while sync is on

profile.name: Profile
profile.help: Picks the voicing: anchors of every group, internal scale of Depth and Warmth

mode.name: Mode
mode.help: Voice topology and its reference settings

depth.name: Depth
depth.help: Peak-to-peak swing of the delay (catalogue chorus.depth: 1 – 8 ms, same meaning)

warmth.name: Warmth
warmth.help: Colour macro: wet low-pass, input saturation, BBD bandwidth and noise, in the profile's proportions

mix.name: Mix
mix.help: Wet level, dry at unity — the catalogue's law (golem forces Calf's dry to 1.0); 1.0 = wet as loud as dry (a CE-2's 50 / 50)

xover_freq.name: Crossover Freq
xover_freq.help: Below this frequency: dry signal, summed to mono

drive.name: Drive
drive.help: Soft saturation of the input stage (wet only)

bbd_chip.name: BBD Chip
bbd_chip.help: Stage count: sets the clock frequency and so the aliasing

bbd_bw.name: BBD Bandwidth
bbd_bw.help: Cut-off of the anti-aliasing and reconstruction filters

emphasis.name: Emphasis
emphasis.help: BBD pre-emphasis before the line and matching de-emphasis after (CE-2: ≈ +15 dB treble shelf); lowers hiss, shapes the BBD's distortion

compander.name: Compander
compander.help: NE570-style compression/expansion (Dimension D): pumping, breathing noise

noise.name: Noise
noise.help: Hiss and clock bleed (BBD), tape hiss (Tape)

mod_custom.name: Modulation Custom
mod_custom.help: Off = follows the profile and the mode

delay_base.name: Base Delay
delay_base.help: Centre delay the modulation swings around

lfo_shape.name: LFO Shape
lfo_shape.help: Triangle is RC-smoothed like the CE-2's (no corner in pitch); Rounded = softer; Random = smoothed random; Log = Strymon "dBucket"-style log LFO

voices.name: Voices
voices.help: Used by Ensemble and Doubler; fixed by the other modes

voice_spread.name: Voice Spread
voice_spread.help: LFO phase offset between successive voices

imperfection.name: Imperfection
imperfection.help: Analogue tolerances: phase and amplitude errors between voices, curved control voltage (string ensembles)

detune_lock.name: Detune Lock
detune_lock.help: Holds the peak pitch deviation constant when Rate changes (depth shrinks as rate rises)

drift.name: Drift
drift.help: Slow random detuning of rate and depth between voices ("human")

crossmix.name: Cross-Mix
crossmix.help: L/R cross-mix of the complementary voices (Dimension mode)

feedback.name: Feedback
feedback.help: Feedback; above ~30 % it drifts towards a flanger

sync.name: Sync
sync.help: Locks the LFO to the host tempo

env_depth.name: Env → Depth
env_depth.help: Playing harder adds (+) or removes (−) depth

env_mix.name: Env → Mix
env_mix.help: Playing harder raises (+) or ducks (−) the wet: chords stay clear on the attack, the chorus blooms on the sustain

stereo_phase.name: Stereo Phase
stereo_phase.help: LFO offset between left and right

mono_safe.name: Mono Safe
mono_safe.help: Complementary voices built so that the mono sum does not hollow out

wet_lpf.name: Wet High Cut
wet_lpf.help: Low-pass on the wet; Warmth moves it around this anchor

mix_law.name: Mix Law
mix_law.help: Add = dry at unity + wet × mix (catalogue); Crossfade = (1 − mix) dry + mix wet (1.0 = vibrato); Equal Power = constant level

level_comp.name: Level Comp
level_comp.help: Static gain computed from mix, the law and the voice count (never from the signal: nothing pumps), so on / off sounds equally loud

presets.name: Classic 80s clean chorus
presets.desc: Single BBD voice, smoothed triangle at 0.8 Hz, wet as loud as dry: deep, warm warble on clean arpeggios

refs.why: Andy Summers' chorus-and-flanger swirl on clean arpeggiated chords

presets.notes: The CE-2 reference (VOICING §6): 50/50 resistor mix = mix 1.0 in the Add law, BBD with emphasis from the profile

presets.name: Synth chorus I
presets.desc: Two 256-stage BBD voices in anti-phase at 0.51 Hz: gentle stereo shimmer that widens pads and polysynth chords

refs.why: Juno-60 layer in the keyboard part, chorus mode on

presets.notes: Measured Juno-60 mode I rate and swing (pendragon-andyh); Keys profile keeps the hiss and drops emphasis like the original

presets.name: Synth chorus II
presets.desc: The same two anti-phase BBD voices at 0.86 Hz: faster, more animated stereo movement on pads and strings
presets.notes: Measured Juno-60 mode II rate; same depth as mode I per the measurement (Arturia says deeper)

presets.name: Synth chorus I+II shimmer
presets.desc: One mono BBD voice at 9.75 Hz with a 0.4 ms swing: a fast, glassy shimmer close to vibrato
presets.notes: Both Juno buttons pressed: measured fast mono mode, tiny swing so the pitch flutters rather than bends

presets.name: Synth-style stereo clean guitar
presets.desc: Juno-type anti-phase stereo voices on a clean guitar: wide, glossy chords that sit beside synth pads
presets.notes: Guitar Clean profile filters (80 Hz to 8 kHz wet) with the Juno topology; warmth 40 opens the top a little

presets.name: Wide still thickener 1
presets.desc: Two complementary companded voices, cross-mixed: width and thickness with almost no audible pitch wobble
presets.notes: Dimension button 1: longest centre delay, subtlest; an always-on spread rather than an effect

presets.name: Wide still thickener 2
presets.desc: Complementary companded voices at half the delay: a tighter, slightly brighter stereo spread without wobble
presets.notes: Dimension button 2: delay about half of mode 1 (manual), same slow rate

presets.name: Wide still thickener 3
presets.desc: Complementary voices with double swing at 0.5 Hz: the most obvious Dimension, still smooth and mono-solid
presets.notes: Dimension button 3: delay between modes 1 and 2, depth doubled (manual)

presets.name: Wide still keys
presets.desc: Dimension-style complementary voices on electric piano, synth or organ: stereo width with the pitch kept still
presets.notes: Keys profile: lows under 100 Hz stay dry and mono, so the left hand stays centred

presets.name: Wide still vocal
presets.desc: Dimension-style voices on a lead or backing vocal at a low mix: width and air, no seasick pitch
presets.notes: Voice profile: clean engine, wet low-cut 150 Hz, mono-safe, wet ducked on syllable attacks

presets.name: High-gain stereo widener
presets.desc: After a high-gain amp: Dimension width on the mids, lows dry and mono, wet ducked on attacks so chugs stay tight
presets.notes: Guitar Drive profile: crossover 150 Hz, wet 250 Hz to 5 kHz, env_mix -30 %; place after amp and cab

presets.name: Stereo clean intro chorus
presets.desc: Bright BBD chorus spread hard left-right on a clean arpeggio before the distorted section hits

refs.why: clean intro through a stereo amp chorus (JC-120 style)

presets.notes: Stereo Custom: opposite LFOs and 130 % wet width mimic a stereo amp chorus; warmth 35 keeps it bright like a solid-state clean

presets.name: Watery grunge chorus
presets.desc: Deep, fairly fast BBD warble on a clean or edge-of-breakup riff: liquid, slightly seasick low strings

refs.why: Small Clone chorus with the depth switch in on the intro riff

presets.notes: Depth 7 ms and 1.3 Hz push past the CE-2 into a deeper, wetter warble; warmth 60 darkens the wet a touch

presets.name: Fuzz wall stereo wash
presets.desc: Deep anti-phase stereo chorus after fuzz, never ducked: chords smear into a wide, warm wall
presets.notes: Modulation Custom only to cancel Guitar Drive's attack ducking (env_mix 0); other values restate the Dual mode anchors

presets.name: Blooming ambient clean chorus
presets.desc: Slow, wide chorus ducked on the pick attack: notes start clear and bloom into movement as they sustain
presets.notes: Envelope ducks wet and depth on attacks (needs Modulation Custom; the rest restates Classic anchors, drift up a little)

presets.name: Electric piano chorus
presets.desc: Warm BBD chorus on electric piano, lows kept dry and centred: the 70s-80s soul and fusion keyboard sheen
presets.notes: Classic single-voice topology through the Keys profile (crossover 100 Hz, no emphasis, a little hiss)

presets.name: Bass chorus, lows untouched
presets.desc: BBD chorus on the mids and highs only: below 200 Hz stays dry and mono, the top end shimmers
presets.notes: Bass profile: crossover 200 Hz, wet low-pass 4 kHz, narrower mono-safe stereo; good on pick bass and chorded lines

presets.name: Fretless studio chorus
presets.desc: Clean digital-style chorus wobble on fretless bass: singing, vocal-like slides with a firm, dry low end

refs.song: Wherever I Lay My Hat (That's My Home)
refs.why: Pino Palladino's fretless line, recorded with Eventide and AMS chorus

presets.notes: Color Custom: clean engine for the 80s rack-digital character instead of BBD; lows still split at 200 Hz by the profile

presets.name: String machine ensemble
presets.desc: Three BBD voices on slow and fast three-phase LFOs: the lush, swirling string-machine ensemble
presets.notes: Ensemble mode: 3 voices, 0.6 Hz + 6 Hz LFOs, 30 % imperfection; also turns a 12-string or organ into a string pad

presets.name: Discreet vocal double
presets.desc: Two randomly wandering voices about 18 ms late at a low mix: a subtle double-track without periodic wobble
presets.notes: Doubler mode: smoothed random paths, no LFO cycle to hear; Voice profile ducks the wet slightly on syllable attacks

presets.name: Worn tape chorus
presets.desc: Chorus on a tape-style line with wow, flutter and hiss: a wobbly, nostalgic, slightly unstable clean tone
presets.notes: Color Custom: Tape engine; wow and flutter add irregular drift on top of the LFO, hiss follows the playing

presets.name: Fast rotary-like warble
presets.desc: Wet-only BBD voice at 5 Hz with a short swing: a fast vibrato-chorus that hints at a spinning speaker
presets.notes: Crossfade law at mix 1.0 = wet only, so it is a vibrato; gfx-rotary is the real speaker model

rate.name: Rate
rate.help: Speed of the sweep (when Sync is Off)

mode.name: Mode
mode.help: The flanger voicing: classic pedals, tape through-zero, barber-pole or pedal-controlled

depth.name: Depth
depth.help: Exponential span between manual and length

fb_polarity.name: Feedback Polarity
fb_polarity.help: Sign of the feedback: + = metallic peaks, − = hollow notches

shape.name: LFO Shape
shape.help: Mode = the mode's own shape; Random = smoothed S&H, fixed seed

sweep_src.name: Sweep Source
sweep_src.help: What sweeps the delay: the LFO, playing dynamics, the Manual control, or LFO and dynamics

env_sens.name: Envelope Sensitivity
env_sens.help: Level at which playing dynamics start to move the sweep

env_att.name: Envelope Attack
env_att.help: How fast the envelope follows a louder note

env_rel.name: Envelope Release
env_rel.help: How fast the envelope falls back after the note

stereo_phase.name: Stereo Phase
stereo_phase.help: LFO offset between left and right (180° = opposite sweeps)

fb_hpf.name: Loop Low Cut
fb_hpf.help: High-pass in the feedback loop: keeps the lows from building up

fb_lpf.name: Loop High Cut
fb_lpf.help: Low-pass in the feedback loop: softens the resonance

presets.name: Silvery BBD flange shimmer
presets.desc: Gentle BBD flanger, moderate regen, 60 % sweep: a shimmering, almost chorus-like swirl on clean chords

refs.why: Alex Lifeson's Electric Mistress shimmer on the clean arpeggios
Andy Summers' flanger-like chord swirl (studio unit disputed)

presets.notes: README application 'Electric Mistress shimmer'; manual/length restate the mode's 0.5 – 8 ms span (they are not set by the mode)

presets.name: Jet-plane hard rock flange
presets.desc: BBD flanger with a log sweep that lingers high and strong regen: the whooshing jet on a cranked riff

refs.why: Eddie's MXR Flanger on the main riff

presets.notes: README 'Jet flanger' starting point; log LFO from the Grey mode, a little loop drive so the regen peaks round off on distortion

presets.name: Galloping driven flange
presets.desc: Faster, resonant BBD flange on a driven, palm-muted gallop: the notes whoosh and growl as the sweep passes

refs.why: Roger Fisher's custom-built flanger on the galloping riff

presets.notes: Shorter length keeps the notches high and metallic; rate 0.45 Hz makes the sweep audible inside a bar

presets.name: Huge slow sweep
presets.desc: Very wide 35:1 BBD sweep at 0.08 Hz: the comb travels from bright fizz down to a deep throat over long phrases
presets.notes: README 'Huge slow sweep'; 0.4 – 14 ms restates the mode's span; loop low cut keeps long delays from booming

presets.name: Cold post-punk flange
presets.desc: Medium-rate BBD flange on bright clean guitar: a cold, glassy, hollow swirl under a repeating figure

refs.why: Mike Hedges stacked several flangers on the guitar

presets.notes: Negative feedback gives hollow notches rather than metallic peaks: colder than the silver shimmer

presets.name: Slow clean intro flange
presets.desc: Slow, deep stereo flange on a clean picked intro: a wide, moving swirl before the heavy part enters
presets.notes: Opposite L/R sweeps (180°) for width on a stereo clean channel

presets.name: Touch-sensitive funk flange
presets.desc: The pick sweeps the flanger: each strum jumps the comb up, it falls back as the note decays
presets.notes: env_sens -25 dB: the sweep starts 30 dB below and tops out at -25 dBFS peaks; lower it for a quiet guitar

presets.name: Expression-pedal flange
presets.desc: No LFO: the foot sweeps the comb through the EXP pedal on Manual, exponential so it moves evenly in pitch
presets.notes: In Pedal mode the delay equals Manual (0.05 – 30 ms): map the EXP pedal to manual; 1 ms puts the first notch at 500 Hz

presets.name: Robotic metallic resonator
presets.desc: A fixed 2 ms comb at near-maximum negative regen: a hollow, ringing robotic resonance on any source
presets.notes: Negative feedback puts peaks at k/τ = 500 Hz multiples; loop drive and filters keep the -2 dB regen safe; EXP on manual retunes it

presets.name: Tape through-zero phrase flange
presets.desc: Two-tape flanging: wet equals dry, the sweep passes through zero and cancels, no regen: the 60s psychedelic whoosh

refs.why: Olympic's tape flanging on the bridge, credited to George Chkiantz

presets.notes: README 'Tape flanging'; Tape TZ delays the dry 1 ms (reported latency); bass_keep is ignored in this mode

presets.name: Through-zero drum bus jet
presets.desc: Through-zero flange with a touch of regen on a drum bus or loop: cymbals and snare sweep in a jet-like whoosh
presets.notes: TZ+ with regen: the zero crossing gives the jet's dramatic cancellation; loop low cut keeps the kick out of the feedback

presets.name: Zero-latency tape-style flange
presets.desc: Near-through-zero flange with the dry all-passed instead of delayed: the tape whoosh live, with no latency
presets.notes: README 'Same, live, no latency'; wet = dry for the deepest cancellation

presets.name: Psychedelic vocal flange
presets.desc: Subtle zero-latency flange on a vocal: a slow, airy phasey sweep on held words, intelligibility kept
presets.notes: Wet -8 dB keeps the cancellation partial so words stay clear; short length keeps the notches in the upper mids and air

presets.name: Bass flange, lows untouched
presets.desc: BBD flange on bass above 150 Hz only: the low end stays dry and mono while the growl and pick sweep
presets.notes: README 'Bass' application: bass_keep 150 Hz complementary split

presets.name: Endless rising flange
presets.desc: Barber-pole flanger: the comb seems to rise forever with no reset, building tension before a drop
presets.notes: README 'Endless rise'; dual crossfaded ramps (Esqueda) so no wrap is heard

presets.name: Endless falling flange
presets.desc: Barber-pole flanger falling forever: a sinking, disorienting sweep for breakdowns and transitions
presets.notes: Slower than the rise: a fall reads better at about 10 s per apparent cycle

presets.name: Two-bar tempo-locked sweep
presets.desc: Log-shaped BBD flange locked to the host: one full sweep every two bars, in phase with the song
presets.notes: README 'Tempo-locked sweep'; phase follows the host position so the peak lands on the same beat every time

rate.name: Rate
rate.help: Speed of the sweep (when Sync is Off)

feedback.name: Feedback
feedback.help: Resonance of the stages (closer to 0 dB = more pronounced)

model.name: Model
model.help: The phaser voicing: classic pedals, Uni-Vibe-style, dual or barber-pole

fb_polarity.name: Feedback Polarity
fb_polarity.help: Sign of the feedback: + = sharper peaks, − = hollow notches

manual.name: Manual
manual.help: Sweep position between low and high; the EXP target

depth.name: Depth
depth.help: How much of the frequency range the sweep covers

skew.name: Skew
skew.help: Tilts the LFO so the sweep rises and falls at different speeds (50 % = symmetric)

sweep_src.name: Sweep Source
sweep_src.help: What sweeps the stages: the LFO, playing dynamics, the Manual control, or LFO and dynamics

env_sens.name: Envelope Sensitivity
env_sens.help: How strongly playing dynamics move the sweep

env_att.name: Envelope Attack
env_att.help: How fast the envelope follows a louder note

env_rel.name: Envelope Release
env_rel.help: How fast the envelope falls back after the note

color.name: Color
color.help: 50 % = the model's own nonlinearity and mismatch (on Stone: its Color switch above 50 %); 0 = ideal

lfo2.name: Second LFO
lfo2.help: Bi-Phase: phaser B follows A, mirrors it, or runs on rate2

routing.name: Routing
routing.help: Bi-Phase: A → B, or A left / B right

lamp_lag.name: Lamp Lag
lamp_lag.help: Response time of the Vibe model's lamp: smoother sweep as it rises

presets.name: Smooth four-stage swirl
presets.desc: Four JFET-style stages, no feedback, slow sine sweep: a smooth, vocal swirl on clean or lightly driven guitar

refs.why: Gilmour moved from the Uni-Vibe to a Phase 90 around 1974

presets.notes: README 'Phase 90 script'; wet = dry for the deepest notches (law dry + wet · phased); mono LFO like the pedal, before the amp

presets.name: Phased hot-rod lead
presets.desc: Feedback-free four-stage phaser in front of a cranked amp: a slow swoosh that adds bite and treble to riffs and solos

refs.why: Eddie's MXR Phase 90 into a cranked amp
Phase 90 on the main riff

presets.notes: Place before the drive/amp: the sweep then shapes what distorts; color 60 adds a little more JFET saturation

presets.name: Pronounced four-stage phase
presets.desc: Four stages with the internal feedback resistor at 1 Hz: a sharper, more resonant, throatier swoosh
presets.notes: README 'Phase 90 block'; the feedback is fixed by the model (the Feedback control is ignored here)

presets.name: Choppy funk rhythm phase
presets.desc: Faster smooth four-stage phase on clean single-note and chord stabs: movement that pulses with sixteenths
presets.notes: Speed near the middle of a Phase 90's knob; range nudged up so the sweep lives in the funk guitar's 500 Hz – 2 kHz

presets.name: Touch-sensitive auto-phase
presets.desc: Picking dynamics sweep a resonant four-stage phaser: each stab quacks up and settles back as it decays
presets.notes: README 'Funk auto-phase'; manual 0 parks the rest position at Low so every attack sweeps upward

presets.name: Slow resonant OTA swirl
presets.desc: Four OTA stages at 0.3 Hz with the color switch's feedback in: a deep, liquid, resonant swirl
presets.notes: README 'Small Stone swirl'; on Stone the colour above 50 % is the feedback (the Feedback control is ignored)

presets.name: Throbbing vibe chorus
presets.desc: Four unequal lamp-driven stages: the pulsing, throbbing, rotary-like vibe swirl in front of a driven amp

refs.why: Uni-Vibe throb at the Fillmore East, Band of Gypsys
Uni-Vibe with a cranked amp, middle pickup

presets.notes: README 'Uni-Vibe' application; place before the amp; the rate drifts up with depth like the original

presets.name: Slow lush vibe
presets.desc: The vibe's unequal stages swept slowly with a lazy lamp: a lush, breathing movement for slow clean or bluesy parts

refs.why: Uni-Vibe in David Gilmour's Dark Side of the Moon-era rig

presets.notes: Longer lamp lag smooths the sweep; tone 45 darkens the wet slightly

presets.name: Mirrored dual stereo phase
presets.desc: Two six-stage phasers, left and right, swept in opposite directions: a wide, three-dimensional phase wall

refs.why: Butch Vig: guitars ran through a Mu-Tron Bi-Phase

presets.notes: README 'Bi-Phase stereo sweep'; Parallel = A left / B right, mirrored LFO; on a mono output both are averaged

presets.name: Bass phase, lows untouched
presets.desc: Smooth four-stage phase on bass above 120 Hz: the growl and slap sweep while the fundamental stays solid
presets.notes: README 'Bass' application; bass_keep 120 Hz complementary split keeps the low end dry and mono

presets.name: Electric piano phase
presets.desc: Slow resonant OTA phase on electric piano or clavinet: the 70s soul and jazz-funk keyboard swirl
presets.notes: Stereo quadrature for keys; bass_keep 100 Hz so the left hand does not swirl

presets.name: Phased string machine
presets.desc: Very slow, resonant OTA phase on string-machine or pad chords: a sweeping, cosmic 70s synth texture

refs.why: string machine through a Small Stone-type phaser

presets.notes: Slower and more resonant than rhodes-phase; pairs with gfx-chorus string-ensemble before it

presets.name: Deep six-octave pad sweep
presets.desc: Twelve stages swept over six octaves at 0.1 Hz with feedback: six notches gliding slowly through a pad
presets.notes: README 'Deep slow sweep'; 100 Hz – 6.4 kHz is exactly six octaves

presets.name: Endless rising phase
presets.desc: Eight-stage barber-pole phaser: the notches climb forever with no audible reset, for builds and risers
presets.notes: README 'Endless rise'; two crossfaded sawtooth cascades

presets.name: Expression-pedal phase
presets.desc: No LFO: six resonant stages swept by the EXP pedal on Manual, a wah-like but hollow vocal sweep
presets.notes: README 'Phase with the foot': map the EXP pedal to manual (0 = Low, 100 = High), exponential and click-free

presets.name: Stepped sample-and-hold phase
presets.desc: Eight resonant stages jumping to a new random position every eighth note, locked to tempo: robotic synth motion
presets.notes: README 'Sample-and-hold phase'; Steps is lightly smoothed so the jumps do not click

presets.name: Psychedelic vocal phase
presets.desc: Gentle four-stage phase at a lower wet level on a vocal: slow, airy movement on sustained words
presets.notes: Wet -6 dB: partial notches keep the words intelligible; bass_keep 150 Hz holds the chest of the voice

presets.name: Phased drum bus
presets.desc: Slow six-stage phase across drums or a loop: cymbals and room swirl while the kick stays dry

refs.why: studio phasing on Bonham's drums

presets.notes: High range up to 8 kHz so the cymbals carry the sweep; bass_keep 150 Hz keeps kick and floor tom solid

speed.name: Speed
speed.help: The footswitch; the ramp is the plugin's, never smoothed by the host

mic.name: Mic Distance
mic.help: Close = dry, aggressive, more AM; far = more reflections

depth.name: Depth
depth.help: Doppler and AM together (100 % ≈ 1.5 × real geometry)

cabinet.name: Cabinet
cabinet.help: The rotary cabinet model: speaker sizes, horn and drum voicing

drive.name: Drive
drive.help: Tube preamp drive before the speakers

balance.name: Horn / Drum
balance.help: Level between the horn (treble) and the drum (bass)

horn_accel.name: Horn Accel
horn_accel.help: Time the horn takes to speed up to Fast

horn_decel.name: Horn Decel
horn_decel.help: Time the horn takes to slow down from Fast to Slow

drum_accel.name: Drum Accel
drum_accel.help: Time the heavier drum takes to speed up to Fast

drum_decel.name: Drum Decel
drum_decel.help: Time the drum takes to slow down from Fast to Slow

counter.name: Counter-rotate
counter.help: Horn and drum in opposite directions

level.name: Level
level.help: Check plain ↔ normalized on REAPER (negative minimum)

presets.name: Organ chorale, slow
presets.desc: Classic two-rotor cabinet at slow speed: gentle Doppler swirl, ready to ramp to fast by footswitch

refs.why: organ-trio tone: tonewheel organ through a spinning cabinet

presets.notes: Stock 122 inertia (horn 0.16/0.32 s, drum 4.1/1.4 s): put speed on a footswitch, the slow-to-fast ramp is the sound

presets.name: Organ fast tremolo
presets.desc: Both rotors at full speed: the shimmering, warbling organ tone for climaxes and fills

refs.why: tonewheel organ riff with a spinning cabinet

presets.notes: Slight horn bias (balance 55) and depth 65 bring the fast warble forward in a band mix

presets.name: Overdriven rock organ
presets.desc: Close-miked cabinet with its tube preamp pushed: growling, gritty organ for hard rock

refs.why: Jon Lord's distorted, aggressive rock organ
Gregg Allman's gritty organ through a spinning cabinet

presets.notes: The crate's organ-growl start: 147 with drive 60+ before the crossover, mic close for more AM and bite

presets.name: Lazy ballad spin-up
presets.desc: Slow cabinet with long, drawn-out speed changes: the swell to fast takes several bars

refs.why: slow, churchy organ swirl carrying the ballad

presets.notes: Ramp 220 % stretches all four time constants: the drum takes ~9 s to reach full speed

presets.name: Gospel quick-switch shout
presets.desc: Punchy cabinet with snappy speed changes and some preamp grit, for stabbing between slow and fast
presets.notes: Ramp 55 % makes the switch answer quickly for church-style speed stabs

presets.name: Guitar drum-rotor warble
presets.desc: Drum-only guitar rotary at fast speed: a thick, liquid warble on clean blues chords

refs.why: rotating-speaker cabinet on the clean rhythm part

presets.notes: The crate's guitar-Leslie start; Vibratone = one rotor, full range, so balance does not matter

presets.name: Warbly grunge verse
presets.desc: Drum-rotor cabinet driven by a cranked amp: a woozy, slightly gritty warble on arpeggios

refs.why: verse guitar through a Leslie 16 powered by a Marshall

presets.notes: Drum fast 5 Hz, a little under stock, gives the lazier warble; more wobble for the drifting feel

presets.name: Wide clean-chord swirl
presets.desc: Far, widely spaced mics at slow speed: lush stereo movement on clean guitar chords

refs.why: Harrison's guitar fed through a rotating speaker

presets.notes: The crate's wide-chords start: mic 85 adds reflections, spacing 85 opens the stereo

presets.name: Subtle rotor thickener
presets.desc: Slow rotary blended under the dry signal: light movement and width that keeps the attack
presets.notes: Mix 40 / depth 40: the dry stays dominant, the cabinet only adds air and motion

presets.name: Spinning-speaker vocal
presets.desc: A voice through a fast rotating cabinet: swirling, distant, otherworldly lead vocal

refs.why: Lennon's vocal re-recorded through a Leslie cabinet
refs.source: Geoff Emerick, Here, There and Everywhere, 2006

presets.notes: Horn-heavy balance keeps the voice intelligible; low drive avoids grit on sibilants

presets.name: Airy rear-cab electric piano
presets.desc: Slow rotary heard from behind the open cabinet: soft, airy swirl on electric piano
presets.notes: Rear cab and far mics trade bite for air, which suits tine pianos better than the front 122

presets.name: Brake to a stop
presets.desc: Rotors coast to a halt with the horn parked at the mic: a dramatic stop to a static, boxy tone
presets.notes: Recall it from a moving speed: brake 60 coasts, stop angle 0° parks the horn facing the mic (brightest)

presets.name: Bass rotor with solid lows
presets.desc: Slow drum rotor on bass, sub-bass kept mono and still, half blended with the dry
presets.notes: Bass keep at its 200 Hz maximum plus mix 60 keep the fundamental steady; only the upper harmonics swirl

presets.name: Mono-safe rotary
presets.desc: Slow/fast cabinet with coincident mics: exactly mono, no hollow sum on a mono PA
presets.notes: Spacing 0 = L equals R: the AM and Doppler survive mono summing on small venue PAs

ceiling.name: Ceiling
ceiling.help: Clip threshold and driven output level

voice.name: Voice
voice.help: The clipping circuit: overdrive, distortion, fuzz or golem's legacy curve

tight.name: Tight
tight.help: Extra pre-clip high-pass on top of the voice's own (metal: 150 – 300 Hz)

asym.name: Asymmetry
asym.help: Bias into the shaper (even harmonics, sputter), DC-blocked after

sag.name: Sag
sag.help: Hard hits lower the gain and move the bias

bass_keep.name: Bass Keep
bass_keep.help: Below it: clean only (a bass keeps its fundamental)

presets.name: Tight boost for high gain
presets.desc: Low-gain mid-hump boost with a 200 Hz pre-clip cut: tightens a high-gain amp's palm mutes

refs.why: a Tube Screamer in front of the Mesa Mark IIC+ rig
a TS-9 used to push and tighten his high-gain amps

presets.notes: A boost, not a drive: the amp distorts, this only cuts the lows and lifts the mids. Keep it ON in high scenes

presets.name: Classic mid-hump overdrive
presets.desc: Tube-Screamer-style overdrive: tight lows, mid hump, the clean signal summed under the clipping
presets.notes: The all-round first drive: into a clean amp it is the distortion, into a crunch amp it adds sustain

presets.name: Texas blues push
presets.desc: Drive nearly off, level up: a mid-forward clean push that makes a crunchy amp sing for solos

refs.why: TS9 with drive low and level near full into a cranked Fender

presets.notes: Little clipping of its own: the high ceiling and summed clean make it a level-and-mids boost; the amp breaks up

presets.name: Transparent edge of breakup
presets.desc: Low-gain drive with 45 % clean blended back: adds hair and level, keeps the guitar's own voice

refs.why: a Klon Centaur on his Wilco pedalboard

presets.notes: The Klon recipe: soft knee plus clean blend; dynamics follow the pick. Good always-on into a clean amp

presets.name: Country chicken-pick snap
presets.desc: Barely-there overdrive with a bright tilt and clean blend: twang with a little hair on hard picks

refs.why: a low-gain signature overdrive into clean Dr. Z amps

presets.notes: Only the hardest picks clip; tone +35 % keeps a Tele's snap over the mid hump

presets.name: Singing overdrive lead
presets.desc: Mid-gain overdrive stacked on a crunchy amp: smooth sustain and a little presence for solos
presets.notes: On a crunch amp it adds sustain rather than fizz; EXP on gain makes a level-matched solo swell

presets.name: Slew-rounded grunge distortion
presets.desc: Hard op-amp distortion with slew-rounded highs: thick, raw rhythm for a clean amp

refs.why: a ProCo RAT on the self-recorded debut

presets.notes: The Distortion voice's slew limit keeps 32 dB of gain from fizzing; tone slightly dark like a RAT's filter past noon

presets.name: Bright distortion into a clean amp
presets.desc: Hard-clipped distortion with a bright tilt, played into a clean channel as the dirty sound

refs.why: a Boss DS-1 into a clean amp channel as the dirty sound

presets.notes: DS-1 territory: harder knee than the RAT preset, brighter tilt; the clean amp adds no gain of its own

presets.name: Punk buzzsaw
presets.desc: Hard, tight distortion with the low end trimmed before the clip: fast down-picked power chords
presets.notes: tight 90 Hz keeps fast chords from blurring; into a clean or barely crunchy amp

presets.name: Classic rock crunch
presets.desc: Medium distortion, neutral tone: a cranked-stack crunch from a clean amp

refs.why: a ProCo RAT among the drives he used on stage

presets.notes: The README's classic crunch: slew-rounded highs, no fizz; back the guitar volume off for rhythm

presets.name: Chainsaw death metal
presets.desc: Maxed distortion, bass trimmed before the clip and highs pushed: the buzzing Swedish chainsaw

refs.why: the Boss HM-2 with every knob up, Stockholm death metal

presets.notes: The pedal is the distortion: into a clean or lightly crunchy amp, not a high-gain one. Tone is a tilt, not the HM-2's EQ

presets.name: Long-sustain fuzz lead
presets.desc: Two-stage fuzz with a darker tone: violin-like sustain for slow melodic solos

refs.why: a Ram's Head Big Muff into a clean Hiwatt for the solos

presets.notes: Pair with a long delay; the clean amp keeps the fuzz smooth rather than gated

presets.name: Wall of fuzz
presets.desc: Saturated two-stage fuzz with a scooped, dark top: a dense wall for heavy alt-rock chords

refs.why: the op-amp Big Muff layered into Marshall heads

presets.notes: Into a crunch amp the fuzz does the saturation and the amp the size; tight 60 Hz keeps stacked chords from booming

presets.name: Fuzz into a loud stack
presets.desc: Big two-stage fuzz with a neutral tone, made to hit a loud, slightly driven stack

refs.why: his first Ram's Head Big Muff into Marshall Super Bass stacks

presets.notes: Loud and woolly; the crunch amp gives the roar. Works for chords and for fuzzed melodic leads

presets.name: Vintage fuzz that cleans up
presets.desc: Biased, saggy fuzz that cleans up when the guitar volume comes down: hairy chords, singing leads

refs.why: a Fuzz Face into cranked Marshalls, volume knob for cleaner tones

presets.notes: Moderate gain and asym/sag make it touch-sensitive: guitar volume at 6 gives a glassy crunch

presets.name: Raw garage blues fuzz
presets.desc: Trebly, slightly sputtering fuzz for blues riffs doubled on guitar and bass

refs.why: an early-70s Ibanez fuzz on guitar and bass since the first record
a Big Muff after the octave-down Whammy

presets.notes: The bias adds even harmonics and a little sputter; bright tilt keeps it cutting in a two-piece band

presets.name: Gated, sputtering fuzz
presets.desc: Heavily biased fuzz that sags and chokes on hard hits: squashed, gated noise-rock texture

refs.why: stacked fuzzes for a squashed, heavily gated tone

presets.notes: The README's sputter recipe: asym 60 % and sag 50 %; notes choke as they decay. Great before reverse reverb

presets.name: Stoner doom fuzz
presets.desc: Maximum two-stage fuzz, very dark tone, full lows: slow, down-tuned riffs into a loud amp

refs.why: fuzz into walls of cranked Orange amps
dark, saturated fuzz for down-tuned doom riffs

presets.notes: Lows left in on purpose (no tight): the riff should rumble. The amp only crunches; the fuzz is the sound

presets.name: Bass overdrive, clean lows
presets.desc: Bass overdrive on the mids with the lows under 150 Hz kept clean and 40 % clean blend

refs.why: mid-forward, overdriven bass that still holds the low end

presets.notes: bass_keep keeps the fundamental mono-solid and phase-aligned; blend restores the attack. Into a clean bass amp or DI

presets.name: Bass fuzz growl
presets.desc: Two-stage fuzz on bass above 120 Hz, clean lows and some clean blend: huge, riff-carrying bass

refs.why: Wolstenholme's fuzz with clean bass blended under it
