fuzzed bass carrying the riffs of a two-piece band

presets.notes: Without bass_keep a fuzz eats the fundamental; 120 Hz keeps the low E and below untouched

presets.name: Modern metal bass grind
presets.desc: Hard bass distortion on the mids only, lows under 100 Hz clean: the clanky modern-metal bass

refs.why: split-band bass: clean lows under a distorted midrange

presets.notes: The bass rig is the amp here, so the class is any: a bass drive stays on in high-gain scenes

presets.name: Rock organ growl
presets.desc: Soft overdrive with a darker tone and some sag: an organ driven through a guitar stack

refs.why: his Hammond C3 driven straight into Marshall amps

presets.notes: Keys have no amp scene of their own: gain any. Darker tone tames the drawbars' upper partials once clipped

presets.name: Electric piano bark
presets.desc: Asymmetric low-gain overdrive: an electric piano barks on hard keystrokes, stays clean when soft
presets.notes: Asymmetry gives the even-harmonic growl of an overdriven Rhodes; the velocity decides how much

presets.name: Legacy golem drive
presets.desc: golem's former JS drive curve at its defaults, now alias-free: old patches sound as before
presets.notes: Compatibility only: the JS block's exact curve without its aliasing. New sounds should use another voice

time.name: Time
time.help: Note value at the host tempo (fallback 120 BPM); Free = time_ms

mix.name: Mix
mix.help: Wet level, dry at unity: linear wet gain = mix / 100 (golem's pct_db law, kept)

model.name: Model
model.help: The delay medium: digital, tape, bucket-brigade or lo-fi

low_cut.name: Low Cut
low_cut.help: In the loop: each repeat thinner

high_cut.name: High Cut
high_cut.help: In the loop, on top of the model's own roll-off: each repeat darker

drive.name: Drive
drive.help: Extra saturation into the loop, on top of the model's own (Echoplex preamp idea)

mod.name: Modulation
mod.help: 50 % = the model's own wow / flutter / chorus; 0 = none; 100 = exaggerated

diffusion.name: Diffusion
diffusion.help: Allpass smear in the loop: repeats blur into a wash (ambient, EchoBoy / Valhalla)

taps.name: Taps
taps.help: Extra playback taps before the feedback point

direction.name: Direction
direction.help: Reverse: each repeat plays backwards, in windows of one delay time, crossfaded at the seams

loop_pitch.name: Loop Pitch
loop_pitch.help: A pitch shifter in the loop: each repeat climbs or falls (crystal delays at +12, shimmer delay at +7 / +12, detuned repeats at ±0.1)

loop_shift.name: Loop Freq Shift
loop_shift.help: A frequency shifter in the loop (±50 Hz, log): repeats drift inharmonically (Valhalla "Ghost"); small values = barber-pole phasing echoes

age.name: Age
age.help: Wear of the medium, per model: Tape = more wow, dropouts, crinkle, treble loss; BBD = more clock noise and compander pumping; Lo-Fi = lower rate and bits;…

swell.name: Swell
swell.help: Auto volume swell into the delay: pick attacks removed from the repeats (pad delays)

sweep.name: Loop Filter Sweep
sweep.help: A slow LFO on the loop's band-pass: each repeat filtered differently (Timeline "Filter")

duck_thresh.name: Duck Threshold
duck_thresh.help: Playing level above which the repeats duck

duck_release.name: Duck Release
duck_release.help: How fast the repeats bloom back

ratio.name: Dual Ratio
ratio.help: Right delay time as a multiple of the left one (Dual stereo mode)

width.name: Width
width.help: Stereo width of the repeats (the dry stays as it is)

hold.name: Hold
hold.help: Freeze: input muted, loop gain 1, saturation bypassed

bypass.name: Bypass
bypass.help: Bypass switch that lets the repeats ring out when Trails is on

trails.name: Trails
trails.help: When bypassed, let the repeats already in the loop fade out naturally

presets.name: Warm analog quarter
presets.desc: Quarter-note bucket-brigade repeats, darker each pass, sitting just behind the playing
presets.notes: All-purpose starting point: BBD darkens the repeats so they never fight the pick; 35 % feedback gives four or five audible echoes

presets.name: Dotted-eighth arena
presets.desc: Dotted-eighth digital repeats as loud as the pick, turning picked eighths into a 16th-note pulse

refs.song: Where the Streets Have No Name
refs.why: the Edge's dotted-eighth echo over muted eighth-note picking
refs.source: Premier Guitar (Electric Etudes: U2's the Edge), 2015

presets.notes: Little feedback and wet about level with the dry, as the lesson describes: the rhythm comes from the echo, so the playing must stay in time

presets.name: Dotted plus quarter cascade
presets.desc: Two delays in one: dotted-eighth and quarter taps interlock into a shimmering 16th-note cascade

refs.why: the Edge stacks a dotted-eighth and a quarter delay for cascading parts
worship guitar convention: dotted-eighth plus quarter under swells

presets.notes: The taps pattern gives both rhythms off one quarter-note time; low cut 150 Hz keeps the cascade off the bass

presets.name: Sun studio slapback
presets.desc: One tape repeat about 135 ms behind the note: the rockabilly and early rock'n'roll slap

refs.why: the Sun-era tape slap on Elvis's early singles
Sun's tape slapback measured at about 134 - 137 ms
refs.source: Tor Halmrast, Art of Record Production conference (via Joe Bennett), 2017

presets.notes: Feedback near zero: one slap, not an echo. Tape loses top and adds a touch of wow like the Ampex machines

presets.name: Tight country slap
presets.desc: A very short, bright single repeat that doubles chicken-picked Telecaster lines

refs.why: Nashville session sound: short slap under fast hybrid picking

presets.notes: Shorter than a rockabilly slap so fast licks stay articulate; low mod keeps the pitch steady on double-stops

presets.name: Single-repeat tape skank
presets.desc: One loud tape repeat on the off-beat, as loud as the chord: reggae-tinged new wave chops

refs.why: Andy Summers's Echoplex single repeat on sparse chords

presets.notes: Guitar World's breakdown gives an EP-3 at about 330 ms, one repeat, half dry / half echo; mix 80 brings the repeat near the dry level

presets.name: Ducked lead echo
presets.desc: Quarter-note repeats that duck under the solo and bloom in the gaps between phrases

refs.why: John Petrucci's lead patches with TC 2290 style dynamic delay
80s studio lead sound: 2290 delay ducked under the line

presets.notes: Ducking 10 dB keeps fast high-gain lines clear; high cut 6.5 kHz removes the fizz from the repeats

presets.name: Floating solo echo
presets.desc: A 440 ms tape-like echo with darker repeats that lifts sustained bends into a big space

refs.why: David Gilmour's solo echo around 440 ms, often under a touch of reverb

presets.notes: 440 ms is the fan-documented starting point, not a sourced setting; pair with a hall at about 2 s

presets.name: Harmony canon echo
presets.desc: Two long repeats at 800 and 1600 ms, one each side, so a solo harmonises with itself

refs.why: Brian May's two delays at 800 and 1600 ms for live canon solos

presets.notes: Dual with ratio 2 gives 800 ms left and 1600 ms right; play phrases that harmonise with themselves two beats later at the song's tempo

presets.name: Three-head tape rhythm
presets.desc: Tape echo with three playback heads at 1/3, 2/3 and 1 of the time: galloping, warbly rhythms

refs.why: Space Echo multi-head echoes at the Black Ark
Jonny Greenwood's tape echo textures on clean parts

presets.notes: The multi-head pattern of an RE-201 style machine; age 30 % adds wow and a little treble loss

presets.name: Dub runaway echo
presets.desc: Dark tape echo near self-oscillation: throws on a snare or a chord that swell into a roar

refs.why: live front-panel echo moves pushing the tape into runaway feedback
Black Ark Space Echo throws and pitch dives

presets.notes: Put feedback on EXP up to 110 % for self-oscillation (bounded); Glide makes time changes dive in pitch like a tape speed knob

presets.name: Backwards solo
presets.desc: Each phrase comes back reversed, wet only: the backwards-guitar solo without tape tricks

refs.why: the reversed-tape guitar solo
reversed guitar solo built from tape

presets.notes: Wet only, no feedback: one reversed copy per half-note window. Play legato; the swell of each window is the sound

presets.name: Reverse halo
presets.desc: Reversed, diffused repeats behind the dry chord: swelling backwards ghosts of what was played

refs.why: reverse delay and looping as part of his clean jazz palette

presets.notes: Feedback 40 % keeps a few reversed passes; diffusion 50 % blurs the window seams into a wash

presets.name: Rising shimmer echo
presets.desc: Each repeat climbs an octave and blurs into a rising pad, with pick attacks swelled out

refs.why: octave-climbing ambient swells behind tremolo-picked leads

presets.notes: The README's Ice-style recipe: shifter plus diffusion in the loop; high cut 5 kHz keeps the octaves from turning shrill

presets.name: Ambient echo wash
presets.desc: Long, diffused, dark repeats that melt into a stereo wash behind chords

refs.why: washes of delay and reverb behind clean chords
oceanic long-feedback delays under bowed guitar

presets.notes: Diffusion 60 % turns echoes into a smear; the 200 Hz - 4 kHz loop band keeps the wash off the dry

presets.name: Long tape accumulator
presets.desc: Four-second tape loop with high feedback: phrases pile up into a slowly decaying drone

refs.why: two-Revox tape delay of several seconds, layered live

presets.notes: Each layer fades over a minute or so; toggle Hold to freeze the loop and play over it

presets.name: Crushed 8-bit echo
presets.desc: Early-digital echo whose repeats lose rate and bits each pass, grainier and grainier
presets.notes: Degradation accumulates per repeat, so the first echo is close to clean and the tail turns to grit

presets.name: Vocal quarter throw
presets.desc: Ping-pong quarter echoes on the voice, filtered and ducked so the words stay dry and clear
presets.notes: Mix-engineer convention: band-limited, ducked throws so the echo only speaks at line ends

presets.name: Fifties vocal slap
presets.desc: A single tape slap about 135 ms behind the voice: the Sun-era rock'n'roll vocal

refs.why: Sam Phillips's tape slap on the Sun singles
refs.source: Tor Halmrast, Art of Record Production conference (via Joe Bennett), 2017

presets.notes: Low cut 200 Hz keeps the slap off the chest tone so it reads as room, not as a double

presets.name: Tape double tracker
presets.desc: A 25 ms modulated copy, no feedback: artificial double tracking that thickens a single take

refs.why: Abbey Road's ADT for Lennon's vocals instead of a second take

presets.notes: The README's ADT recipe: wow on the copy is what makes it read as a second take rather than a comb

presets.name: Bass eighth halo
presets.desc: Eighth-note repeats on the bass with the lows cut from the loop: melodic lines echo, the low end stays solid

refs.why: Peter Hook's high melodic bass lines under echo and chorus

presets.notes: Low cut 350 Hz in the loop: only the mids and upper harmonics repeat, so the fundamental is never smeared

presets.name: Synth ping-pong
presets.desc: Dotted-eighth ping-pong across the stereo field: arpeggios bounce left and right

refs.why: wide, long echoes on CS-80 leads and arpeggios

presets.notes: Classic synth-pop dotted bounce; the 150 Hz loop low cut keeps bass notes mono and dry

mix.name: Mix
mix.help: Wet level, dry at unity (catalogue law)

decay.name: Decay
decay.help: Time the tail takes to fall by 60 dB in the mid band

size.name: Size
size.help: Size of the room: longer early reflections and a bigger tail

predelay.name: Predelay
predelay.help: golem pins it at insert for blocks that do not expose it (hall: 15 ms, room: 5 ms)

hicut.name: High Cut
hicut.help: Damping (RT60 halves there) + a gentle output low-pass

algo.name: Algorithm
algo.help: Pinned by golem per block (the first three are today's blocks)

bass_xover.name: Bass Crossover
bass_xover.help: Frequency below which Bass Mult scales the decay

mod.name: Modulation
mod.help: 50 % = the algorithm's own depth; 0 = static (may ring); 100 = lush, towards chorus

diffusion.name: Diffusion
diffusion.help: How quickly the echoes blur into a smooth tail

early.name: Early Reflections
early.help: 50 % = the algorithm's own level; ignored on Plate

width.name: Width
width.help: Stereo width of the tail (above 100 % = wider than the room)

era.name: Era
era.help: The converter and the modulation of the period (VintageVerb's "Color"): the tail runs at a reduced internal rate behind 4-pole converters

mod_rate.name: Modulation Rate
mod_rate.help: 50 % = the algorithm's own (Lexicon "spin"); mod is the depth ("wander")

high_mult.name: High Decay
high_mult.help: High-band RT60 ratio above hicut / 2: with bass_mult, a three-band decay

wet_low.name: Wet Low Shelf
wet_low.help: ±12 dB at 200 Hz on the wet

wet_high.name: Wet High Shelf
wet_high.help: ±12 dB at 4 kHz on the wet: tone of the reverb without changing its decay

swell.name: Swell
swell.help: Auto volume swell into the reverb: the pick attack is removed from the wet (pad / violin effect)

drive.name: Drive
drive.help: Saturation into the tank; on Spring = dwell

springs.name: Springs
springs.help: Number of springs in the Spring algorithm

sync.name: Sync
sync.help: Predelay (and Gated / Reverse length) as a note value

shimmer.name: Shimmer
shimmer.help: Share of the tail fed back through a pitch shifter (gfx-shimmer's regeneration insert, one voice): each pass climbs by shimmer_pitch

duck.name: Ducking
duck.help: How much the tail drops while you play

duck_release.name: Duck Release
duck_release.help: How fast the tail comes back once you stop

freeze.name: Freeze
freeze.help: Freeze = the tail holds, new notes stay out; Infinite = the tail holds and new notes add to it

kill_dry.name: Kill Dry
kill_dry.help: Mutes the direct signal, for parallel routing

bypass.name: Bypass
bypass.help: Bypass switch that lets the tail ring out when Trails is on

trails.name: Trails
trails.help: When bypassed, let the tail already in the room decay naturally

presets.name: Lush clean hall
presets.desc: A three-second modulated hall that wraps clean arpeggios without a metallic ring
presets.notes: The README's clean-arpeggio recipe; mod 70 % keeps a long tail smooth, hicut 6 kHz keeps it behind the pick

presets.name: Ducked lead hall
presets.desc: A 2.2 s hall with 40 ms predelay that steps back while the solo plays and blooms in the gaps

refs.why: David Gilmour's solo tone: delay into a moderate hall

presets.notes: Predelay keeps the attack dry and in front; 6 dB ducking stops the tail from washing out high-gain notes

presets.name: Eighties digital hall
presets.desc: A long, slightly grainy period hall with deep chorusing modulation for 80s ballads

refs.why: Lexicon-era big digital hall on synths and guitars
early-digital hall reverbs across the album

presets.notes: Era 80s: reduced bandwidth and converter grain of early digital units; the README's 80s ballad recipe

presets.name: Dark seventies hall
presets.desc: A warm, band-limited early-digital hall whose tail sits low and soft behind the band

refs.why: the Lexicon 224 hall era of late-70s and early-80s records

presets.notes: 70s era runs the tail at 20 kHz with 10-bit input; the wet high shelf at 35 % darkens without shortening the decay

presets.name: Octave shimmer hall
presets.desc: A long hall fed back through an octave-up shifter: each pass climbs into a glowing halo

refs.why: pitch shifter at +1 octave in a feedback loop with a long reverb
the shimmer heard on The Unforgettable Fire

presets.notes: Shimmer 40 % with a 7 s decay: the octave grows audibly over a few seconds; for two voices and glide use gfx-shimmer

presets.name: Endless cloud
presets.desc: A 30-second, heavily diffused cloud that turns any note into a slow drone, ducked under the playing

refs.why: bowed guitar into vast reverb, building walls of sound
endless drones of reverberated guitar and strings

presets.notes: The README's post-rock wall: low cut and bass decay 0.7x keep 30 s of tail from turning into mud

presets.name: Blooming pad
presets.desc: A reverb that fades in behind each note while the pick attack is removed: guitar becomes a pad

refs.why: worship pad guitars: volume-swelled notes into a huge blooming verb

presets.notes: Bloom fades the tail in, swell removes the attacks from the wet: the dry still plays, the pad grows behind it

presets.name: Dripping surf spring
presets.desc: A hard-hit three-spring tank: the splashy drip of surf lead and twang

refs.why: drenched spring reverb on staccato tremolo-picked surf leads
wet surf guitar drip

presets.notes: Drive is dwell on Spring: 65 % hits the springs hard for the drip; mix high, as surf players set the tank near the top

presets.name: Amp spring, low
presets.desc: A gentle two-spring amp reverb, short and low in the mix: the built-in combo reverb at 2 or 3
presets.notes: Low dwell avoids the drip: the spring is felt as space, not heard as an effect

presets.name: Dub spring crash
presets.desc: A dark, overdriven spring for dub: rimshots and skanks thrown into a crashing tank

refs.why: spring reverb slams and throws in the dub mix
Black Ark spring reverb alongside the Space Echo

presets.notes: High dwell makes the tank crash on transients; put mix on EXP for throws

presets.name: Reverse wall
presets.desc: Wet-only reverse reverb: every chord swells in backwards and melts, the dry guitar removed

refs.why: Kevin Shields: reverse reverb on an SPX90, no dry guitar signal

presets.notes: Shields says he uses purely the reverb, none of the dry: kill dry on, mix 100 %. Pair with tremolo-arm bends

presets.name: Eighties gated burst
presets.desc: A dense, flat burst cut dead on the eighth note: huge gated drums and stabs

refs.why: compressed room mic gated about a second after each hit
the first gated-drum sound with Padgham and Collins

presets.notes: Played without cymbals, as Padgham asked Collins: the gate closes the burst on the grid. Also works on guitar stabs

presets.name: Air around the amp
presets.desc: Early reflections only, no tail: always-on air and width around a dry amp sim
presets.notes: Ambience is space without a tail: safe on high gain and tight rhythm, where a hall would smear the palm mutes

presets.name: Classic vocal chamber
presets.desc: A warm 1.8 s chamber with a short predelay: the crooner's echo room

refs.why: Capitol Studios' underground echo chambers on his 50s ballads

presets.notes: Chamber: dense early reflections and a smooth tail; low modulation keeps sustained vowels steady in pitch

presets.name: Piano chamber
presets.desc: A 1.5 s chamber with little modulation: space around piano and keys without pitch wobble
presets.notes: The README's keys recipe: low modulation, as chorusing is obvious on sustained piano

presets.name: Vocal plate
presets.desc: A bright 1.4 s plate with 20 ms predelay and low cut: dense sheen behind a lead vocal

refs.why: Abbey Road's EMT 140 plates behind mid-period vocals

presets.notes: Plate gives instant density; low cut 150 Hz and predelay keep consonants clear

presets.name: Snare plate
presets.desc: A one-second bright plate for snare and toms: the classic drum plate
presets.notes: Plate programs were all over 80s drums (Sound On Sound, 2011, on the Lexicon 224); short decay keeps the groove

presets.name: Octave halo plate
presets.desc: A two-second plate with a faint octave shimmer: a glow on clean arpeggios
presets.notes: Shimmer 25 % is a colour, not the subject; the plate's instant density suits picked notes

presets.name: Short soul plate
presets.desc: A short, tight plate low in the mix: lift for funk and soul chops without blurring the groove
presets.notes: Under a second so 16th-note scratches stay percussive

presets.name: Amp in a room
presets.desc: A 0.7 s room with dense early reflections: a dry amp sim sounds miked in a real space
presets.notes: The README's room recipe; works on crunch and high gain where long tails smear

presets.name: Live drum room
presets.desc: A 0.8 s room with strong early reflections: kit ambience for jazz, indie and rock drums
presets.notes: Early reflections at 70 % give the room mic sound; the tail stays short

presets.name: Bass room touch
presets.desc: A half-second room on the highs only: space for bass without smearing the low end
presets.notes: Low cut 250 Hz into the reverb: only the attack and harmonics reverberate

decay.name: Decay
decay.help: Time the tail takes to fall by 60 dB in the mid band

shimmer.name: Shimmer
shimmer.help: Share of shifted signal in the loop

pitch2.name: Pitch 2
pitch2.help: Interval of the second pitch voice

voice2.name: Voice 2 Level
voice2.help: Level of the second pitch voice

detune.name: Detune
detune.help: Detunes the two sides apart for a wider, chorused shimmer

size.name: Size
size.help: Scale of the reverb tank: bigger = slower, wider space

bloom.name: Bloom
bloom.help: Diffusion; mid values fade in slowly

moddepth.name: Modulation
moddepth.help: Low by default: the shifter already modulates

space.name: Space
space.help: Which gfx-reverb tail carries the shimmer: Cloud = the biggest and slowest (ValhallaShimmer's large modes), Plate = tight and bright

swell.name: Swell
swell.help: Auto volume swell into the reverb: no pick attack in the pad (Mercury7)

voice_pan.name: Voice Spread
voice_pan.help: Voice 1 towards the left, voice 2 towards the right

bass_mult.name: Bass Decay
bass_mult.help: Low-frequency decay relative to the mid band

glide.name: Pitch Glide
glide.help: Time for pitch / pitch2 to reach a new value: scene changes sweep instead of jumping

freeze.name: Freeze
freeze.help: Freeze = the pad holds, the climb stops (shifter out of the loop), new notes stay out; Infinite = the pad holds and new notes add to it

kill_dry.name: Kill Dry
kill_dry.help: Mutes the direct signal, for a parallel lane

trails.name: Trails
trails.help: When bypassed, let the tail decay naturally

bypass.name: Bypass
bypass.help: Bypass switch that lets the tail ring out when Trails is on

presets.name: Classic octave shimmer
presets.desc: Octave-up shifter in the hall's loop: each pass climbs an octave into a long, rolled-off halo

refs.why: Eno and Lanois's octave-up shifter in a reverb feedback loop
the Eno/Lanois shimmer featured on the 1984 album

presets.notes: The recipe: +12 in the feedback, long decay, highs rolled off on the return (hicut 6 kHz) so the climb fades instead of hissing

presets.name: Subtle sparkle
presets.desc: A little octave-up in a 3 s hall at 25 % mix: clean chords gain air without a wash
presets.notes: Low shimmer share = few octave passes: shine, not a pad

presets.name: Organ halo
presets.desc: Reverse-grain octave and twelfth voices in the loop: a smooth, organ-like halo over sustained chords
presets.notes: Smooth = reverse grains (Valhalla's 'organ-like' mode); pitch2 +19 adds the twelfth like an organ's quint stop

presets.name: Cinematic fifths
presets.desc: Fifth and octave voices climbing in a cathedral: an open, heroic pad under slow chords
presets.notes: Fifths climb fast through the harmonic series; keep the chords sparse or they turn to mush

presets.name: Dark descent
presets.desc: Octave-down shifter in the loop with a high low cut: the tail sinks instead of climbing
presets.notes: lowcut 200 Hz and bass_mult 0.8 stop each downward pass from piling up as mud

presets.name: Octave halo, no climb
presets.desc: Shifter on the input only: the tail sits one octave up and never runs away, behind melodic leads
presets.notes: Input placement does not climb (Strymon's Input mode): safe on busy leads; duck 30 % keeps notes clear

presets.name: Ducked swell pad
presets.desc: Octave shimmer that ducks while you play and blooms in the gaps: a pad that stays out of the way

refs.why: worship guitar pads of swells and octave shimmer under the band

presets.notes: duck 50 % + bloom 60 %: the wash fades in slowly and backs off under the pick

presets.name: Attack-free strings
presets.desc: Auto-swell into a reverse-grain octave tail, wet-heavy: picked notes come in like bowed strings
presets.notes: Swell 500 ms removes the pick attack inside the reverb (Mercury7 idea), so no volume pedal is needed

presets.name: Giant cloud
presets.desc: Octave shimmer in the biggest, slowest space with a 12 s tail: an enormous, diffuse pad
presets.notes: ValhallaShimmer-style large mode; bloom 60 % fades the tail in slowly

presets.name: Octaves up and down
presets.desc: Octave-up and octave-down voices together in the loop: the tail spreads both ways like an organ full stop
presets.notes: Valhalla's 'Dual'. lowcut 220 Hz is needed: the down voice otherwise piles up lows on every pass

presets.name: Bright plate shimmer
presets.desc: Short, bright plate with some octave-up: tight shimmer that suits strummed rhythm parts
presets.notes: A 2 s plate gives only a few climbs before the tail dies: shimmer that keeps time

presets.name: Infinite growing wash
presets.desc: Infinite hold: the shimmer pad never decays and every new note adds to it, for drones and outros
presets.notes: Put freeze on a footswitch to release it. For a held chord that stops climbing, switch freeze to Freeze

presets.name: Interval-sweeping pad
presets.desc: Fifth-up shimmer with a 1 s pitch glide: a scene change to another interval sweeps the whole pad
presets.notes: Scenes set pitch +7 → +12 (or −12); glide 1 s turns the jump into a sweep

presets.name: Vocal octave air
presets.desc: Light octave shimmer behind a voice, 80 ms predelay and ducked: an airy halo that keeps words clear
presets.notes: Predelay and ducking keep consonants dry; lowcut 300 Hz keeps the chest of the voice out of the climb

presets.name: Keys cloud pad
presets.desc: Octave and fifth voices in a cloud, soft swell: piano or synth chords bloom into an endless pad
presets.notes: A short swell softens piano hammers before they reach the tank

presets.name: Heavy-wall shimmer
presets.desc: Ducked octave shimmer with a high low cut behind distorted guitars: a glowing halo over a wall of riffs
presets.notes: Distortion before shimmer climbs harsh fast: hicut 5 kHz and lowcut 350 Hz keep only the glow, duck lets the riff through

depth.name: Depth
depth.help: How far the signal drops when cut (100 % = silence)

sync.name: Sync
sync.help: Note value of the stutter at the host tempo; Free = the Rate control

trigger.name: Trigger
trigger.help: What starts the stutter: engaging the pedal, each pick attack, or the beat

sens.name: Sensitivity
sens.help: Sensitivity of the pick detector (Trigger = Pick)

smooth.name: Smooth
smooth.help: Edge crossfade, clamped to the segment; 0 = hard cut

shape.name: Shape
shape.help: Envelope of each cut: hard gate or a smoother waveform

swing.name: Swing
swing.help: Delays every other step for a shuffled rhythm

offset.name: Offset
offset.help: Grid shift, in fractions of a step

kill.name: Kill
kill.help: Momentary: hold to mute (with the edge crossfade)

restart.name: Restart
restart.help: Each off → on edge restarts the pattern

presets.name: Standard 1/16 stutter
presets.desc: Full cuts on every 1/16 at the song tempo, half of each step open, de-clicked edges; starts when engaged
presets.notes: golem's Standard kept: the pattern restarts on each engage, so a stomp on the beat lines it up

presets.name: Hand-played kill switch
presets.desc: Passes audio untouched until the Kill footswitch is held, then mutes with a near-hard edge: a played toggle stutter

refs.why: Tom Morello flicks between a dead and a live pickup to stutter notes

presets.notes: Depth 0: the pattern never cuts; only the momentary Kill (on a footswitch) mutes. Smooth 0.3 ms keeps the clack without a pop

presets.name: Rapid button flutter
presets.desc: Hard 16 Hz on-off chop, free-running, no edge smoothing: a kill button tapped as fast as possible over legato runs

refs.why: right hand on a hard-wired kill switch while the left hand taps legato

presets.notes: Smooth 0 is a true hard cut: the click is part of the sound. EXP on rate (1-30 Hz) plays the tapping speed by foot

presets.name: Machine-gun helicopter
presets.desc: Free-running 14 Hz chop with 40 % open steps: a helicopter or machine-gun rattle on held notes
presets.notes: golem's Machine Gun kept; free rate because the rattle should not lock to the song

presets.name: Song-locked 1/16 stutter
presets.desc: Hard 1/16 cuts locked to the host's bar position, step 1 on the downbeat: a tight rhythmic stutter on chords
presets.notes: Beat trigger follows the transport, so the cuts stay on the click even after a loop or a seek

presets.name: Engaged 1/16 stutter
presets.desc: Hard 1/16 cuts that start the moment the pedal is stomped, 45 % open: a fast stutter on a held chord
presets.notes: golem's Stutter 1/16 kept

presets.name: Pick-restarted triplet stutter
presets.desc: 1/16-triplet cuts that restart on every pick attack: each strum gets its own stutter, wherever it falls
presets.notes: golem's Pick Stutter kept; raise sens for light picking, lower it if low-string ripple retriggers

presets.name: Syncopated trance gate
presets.desc: 1/16 gate on the pattern x.xx.x.xx.xx.xx., locked to the bar, soft 3 ms edges: chops a held pad into a riff

refs.why: early stuttering gated synth chords on a mid-90s dance hit

presets.notes: Pattern 28077 = steps 1,3,4,6,8,9,11,12,14,15; length 70 % lets steps that follow each other almost join

presets.name: Four-on-the-floor pump
presets.desc: Quarter-note ramp-up swell locked to the beat, 70 % deep: the sidechain duck of a kick, without a kick

refs.why: the whole track pumps against the kick like a sidechain duck

presets.notes: Ramp Up drops at each beat and swells back, depth in dB so it sounds even; works on pads, bass, or a whole guitar bus

presets.name: Accented 1/16 groove
presets.desc: 1/16 chop where only beats 1-4 cut fully and other steps dip by 60 % of 70 %: a pulse with a downbeat
presets.notes: Accent 4369 = steps 1,5,9,13 (the beats) at full depth; other steps cut at depth x 0.6, so the groove breathes instead of chopping

presets.name: Swung eighth slicer
presets.desc: 1/8 cuts with 30 % swing and soft edges: a shuffled, head-nodding chop on chords or samples
presets.notes: Swing lengthens the on-beat eighth and shortens the off-beat one; 30 % sits near a triplet shuffle

presets.name: Tempo-locked sine tremolo
presets.desc: Smooth sine level wobble on 1/8 notes, 60 % deep, locked to the song: a tremolo that never drifts off tempo
presets.notes: For an amp-style photocell or bias tremolo use gfx-tremolo; this one is for a tremolo that must stay on the grid

presets.name: Reverse-like quarter swells
presets.desc: Full-depth ramp-up on each quarter note: every beat fades in from silence, like a tape played backwards
presets.notes: Best before a reverb or delay so the swells blur together; Engage restarts the cycle on the stomp

presets.name: Breakdown rhythm chop
presets.desc: Hard 1/16 cuts on the pattern x.x..x.xx..x.x.., bar-locked: turns a held chord into a syncopated breakdown riff
presets.notes: Pattern 10661 = steps 1,3,6,8,9,12,14; length 80 % keeps each hit full like a palm-muted chug, near-hard edges

presets.name: Triplet bass chop
presets.desc: 1/16-triplet gate on every other step, bar-locked, hard edges: a rolling wobble-like chop on a sustained bass
presets.notes: 12 steps of 1/16T = one bar; pattern 18761 opens steps 1,4,7,9,12 for a lopsided triplet roll (bits above 12 ignored)

presets.name: Eighth-note bass chop
presets.desc: Full 1/8 cuts with 60 % open steps and 2 ms edges: a sustained bass note turned into driving eighths
presets.notes: golem's Bass Chop kept; 2 ms edges stop low notes from clicking at each cut

presets.name: Half-depth eighth chop
presets.desc: 1/8 dips of 70 % instead of silence: a choppy pulse that keeps the sustain underneath
presets.notes: golem's Half Chop kept

presets.name: Syllable vocal stutter
presets.desc: 1/16 cuts that restart on each sung onset, 45 % open, 2 ms edges: chops words into stuttered syllables

refs.why: stuttered vocal syllables used as the hook

presets.notes: golem's Vocal Stutter kept; sens 40 so breaths and consonants do not retrigger

presets.name: Build-up 1/32 roll
presets.desc: Hard 1/32 chop locked to the bar on drums or a full mix: the stuttered roll before a drop
presets.notes: Put it on a scene for the last bar before the drop, or EXP on length to tighten the roll as the build rises

presets.name: Ping-pong triplet stutter
presets.desc: 1/8-triplet cuts alternating left and right at full width: the stutter bounces across the stereo field
presets.notes: Width needs the stereo layout: the right channel runs half a step behind, so one side opens as the other closes

octave1.name: Octave -1
octave1.help: Level of the voice one octave below

octave2.name: Octave -2
octave2.help: Level of the voice two octaves below

octave_up.name: Octave +1
octave_up.help: Level of the voice one octave above

mode.name: Mode
mode.help: Tracking engine and character: vintage analog, clean, synth-like or polyphonic

instrument.name: Instrument
instrument.help: Input filter (800 / 300 Hz) and trigger time constants

sub_tone.name: Sub Tone
sub_tone.help: Low-pass on −1 oct; −2 oct follows at ~0.45×

up_tone.name: Up Tone
up_tone.help: Low-pass on the octave-up voice: tames its harshness

sensitivity.name: Sensitivity
sensitivity.help: Hysteresis and gate relative to the envelope

glide.name: Glide
glide.help: Pitch glide between notes, for a synth-like octave

range.name: Range
range.help: Poly: only notes below this get octaved

presets.name: Analog octave down
presets.desc: Analog-style divider adds a sub one octave below at 70 % under the full dry: fatter single-note riffs

refs.why: octave-thickened single-note desert riffs

presets.notes: golem's OC-2 classic. Zero latency; single notes, neck pickup tracks best

presets.name: Guitar synth-bass line
presets.desc: Dry low, octave and two-octaves-down subs loud: a single-note guitar plays a glitchy-warm synth bass

refs.why: a guitar riff dropped an octave to stand in for a bass

presets.notes: golem's Sub synth. The record used a Whammy an octave down; the divider's ÷4 voice adds the synth-like floor

presets.name: Clean bass sub
presets.desc: Near-sine sub an octave below that follows the bass player's dynamics, under the full dry
presets.notes: Clean mode: half-angle sub, 3rd harmonic under −50 dBc, no tracking glitches on decays. sub_tone 250 Hz keeps only the fundamental

presets.name: Funk octave-divider bass
presets.desc: Analog divider sub at 60 % on bass, a little rough: the 1970s octave-divided funk bass

refs.why: a Mu-Tron Octave Divider in his bass rig
octave-divided funk bass lines

presets.notes: Pair with gfx-autowah after it for the envelope-filter funk sound

presets.name: Glide synth bass
presets.desc: Divider-locked oscillator, mostly square, gliding 40 ms between notes, dry muted: a bass becomes a synth
presets.notes: Synth: phase-locked to the divider (zero latency), a YIN gate mutes uncertain input. Legato lines show off the glide

presets.name: Octave-up fuzz lead
presets.desc: Rectifier octave up loud over half the dry, into a fuzz: a ringing, ring-mod-like octave lead

refs.why: the Octavia's octave-up on the solo

presets.notes: Place it before a fuzz; neck pickup above the 12th fret makes the octave bloom most

presets.name: Polyphonic organ stack
presets.desc: Polyphonic octave down, two down and one up with the dry: chords and riffs turn into a pipe-organ stack

refs.why: Jack White's octave-layering POG for an organ-like guitar

presets.notes: golem's Organ stack, moved to Poly so chords work; range 1000 Hz octaves every note

presets.name: Sub on the bass note
presets.desc: Polyphonic sub only on notes under 150 Hz: chords keep their voicing, the root gets an octave below
presets.notes: range 150 Hz = the low strings only (the OC-5 'Lowest' idea), for a band without a bassist

presets.name: Polyphonic octave sparkle
presets.desc: Polyphonic octave up at half level over the dry: clean chords gain a 12-string, organ-like shine
presets.notes: Zero latency per-band doubling; gfx-pitch twelve-string adds detune but costs 6.6 ms

presets.name: Bass plays guitar
presets.desc: Polyphonic octave up loud on bass with the dry kept: one bass covers both the riff's guitar and low end

refs.why: Mike Kerr's octave-up bass split to guitar and bass amps

presets.notes: Ideally on a split lane: octave voice to a guitar amp, dry to a bass amp. Poly so double-stops work

presets.name: Doom sub floor
presets.desc: Clean sub one and two octaves below the full dry: a riff gains a seismic floor under the drive
presets.notes: Place before the drive; Clean subs stay sine-like, so the amp's distortion adds the grit. sensitivity 40 % gates decays

presets.name: Square-wave synth lead
presets.desc: Divider-locked square oscillator below plus a rectified octave up, little dry: a chiptune-style lead
presets.notes: sub_tone fully open lets the square's harmonics through; single notes on the neck pickup

presets.name: Keys left-hand sub
presets.desc: Polyphonic sub only under 200 Hz: a keyboard's left hand gets a clean octave below, the right hand untouched
presets.notes: instrument Bass gives the 300 Hz input filter and slower trigger constants that suit sustained keyboard bass notes

shift.name: Shift
shift.help: Smoothed in semitones (≈ 10 ms one-pole + slew limit), converted per sample

mix.name: Mix
mix.help: Equal-power dry / wet; the dry is delayed by the reported latency so the mix stays coherent

engine.name: Engine
engine.help: Whammy: single notes, pitch-synchronous splices, 12 ms

tracking.name: Tracking
tracking.help: Poly synthesis window: Fast = 6.6 ms (tighter, a partial ~0.5 dB less on its target); Stable = 10 ms

glide.name: Glide
glide.help: Time for shift to reach a new value (heel-to-toe dives)

voice2.name: Voice 2 Level
voice2.help: Level of the second pitch voice

fine.name: Fine
fine.help: Fine tuning of voice 1 (detuned doubles, tuning to a recording)

harmony.name: Harmony
harmony.help: Scale: shift and shift2 become scale steps above the played note (see below); glide is not used

key.name: Key
key.help: golem knows the song's key and can set it per song

presets.name: Octave-wide bends
presets.desc: Mono shifter, fully wet, toe at an octave up: an expression pedal bends a held note a whole octave

refs.why: Gilmour's octave-wide bends with a Whammy

presets.notes: Put the expression pedal on shift 0 → +12; glide 0 so the pedal is the bend. Single notes only

presets.name: Two octaves up, crawling
presets.desc: Mono shifter, fully wet, two octaves up with a slow glide: a screaming, straining solo voice

refs.why: Morello's solo with the Whammy set two octaves up

presets.notes: glide 300 ms makes a scene switch crawl up to +24 rather than jump; with an expression pedal on shift, set glide 0

presets.name: Octave-down bass riff
presets.desc: Mono shifter, fully wet, one octave down: a single-note guitar riff turns into a bass line

refs.why: the riff dropped an octave with a Whammy to sound like a bass

presets.notes: Fully wet: the dry note would give it away. Neck pickup and single notes; off for the full chords of the chorus

presets.name: Two-octave dive
presets.desc: Mono shifter, fully wet, two octaves down reached over 600 ms: a dive-bomb growl from any note

refs.why: Whammy settings from two octaves up to two down across the record

presets.notes: Glide makes the scene change a dive; the 12 ms Whammy engine keeps the attack tight at −24

presets.name: Octave-up squealing riff
presets.desc: Mono shifter, fully wet, an octave up on a high-gain riff: squealing, harmonic-like pitch jumps

refs.why: Dimebag's Whammy on the main riff for squealing jumps

presets.notes: Same voice as octave-up-bends, meant for a riff rocked on and off the toe with the expression pedal after the drive

presets.name: Octave-down riff thickener
presets.desc: Mono shifter an octave down mixed 40 % under the dry: heavier single-note riffs without a bass
presets.notes: The dry is delayed by the 12 ms latency so the blend stays coherent. For a synth-like sub use gfx-octaver

presets.name: Octave-down chords
presets.desc: Polyphonic shifter an octave down at half mix: whole chords gain a low octave, Stable window
presets.notes: Poly handles power chords and open chords; Stable (10 ms) keeps low partials on target

presets.name: Down a half step
presets.desc: Polyphonic shifter, fully wet, one semitone down: E-standard guitar plays in E-flat tuning
presets.notes: Virtual capo for songs tuned down a half step; Fast tracking (6.6 ms) for feel. fine can match a slightly detuned record

presets.name: Down a whole step
presets.desc: Polyphonic shifter, fully wet, two semitones down: D-standard without retuning

presets.name: Baritone drop
presets.desc: Polyphonic shifter, fully wet, a fourth down, Stable window: a six-string plays in B standard
presets.notes: Stable for the low register; put it before the amp so the drive sees the low note

presets.name: Electric 12-string
presets.desc: Polyphonic octave up at 35 % with 5 cents of detune: a six-string strums like a 12-string

refs.why: the jangling 12-string sound this imitates on a six-string

presets.notes: fine +5 ct keeps the octave from fusing with the dry, as real octave strings drift

presets.name: Fixed fifth stack
presets.desc: Mono shifter a fifth up at 45 %: single notes become power-chord dyads
presets.notes: Fixed interval, so it stays parallel (not in key): right for riffs, wrong for melodic leads (see twin-lead-third)

presets.name: In-key twin lead
presets.desc: A diatonic third above every note, in the song's key, at half mix: one guitar plays twin harmony leads

refs.song: The Boys Are Back in Town
refs.why: twin guitar leads a third apart (played by two guitarists)
harmonized twin-guitar melodies in thirds

presets.notes: Scale: shift 4 = a third in the scale; golem sets key / scale per song (E minor is the placeholder). Single notes; bends hold the old interval

presets.name: Three-voice harmony lead
presets.desc: A diatonic third and fifth above the played note in key: a three-part harmonized lead

refs.why: an H3000 harmonizer user who contributed its signature presets
Brian May's three-part guitar harmonies (multitracked)

presets.notes: Scale: shift 4 = third, shift2 7 = fifth above. Key placeholder; voice 2 −4 dB keeps the third as the main harmony

presets.name: Stacked octaves organ
presets.desc: Polyphonic octave down and octave up together at half mix: chords become an organ-like stack
presets.notes: Works on guitar chords too; the octave up 6 dB under the octave down keeps the stack warm

presets.name: Bass octave-up lead
presets.desc: Mono shifter an octave up at 60 % on bass: a fills and lead voice that cuts like a guitar
presets.notes: Single notes. For a bass that keeps its low end and adds a guitar-like octave, gfx-octaver's octave_up is the lower-latency option

shift.name: Shift
shift.help: Smoothed in semitones (≈ 10 ms one-pole + slew limit), converted per sample

search.name: Splice Search
search.help: WSOLA-style splice point (H3000 "deglitch"); on adds a fixed lookahead

presets.name: Deglitched octave down
presets.desc: Two-head shifter an octave down with splice search, blended under the dry: a smooth lower double
presets.notes: Long window and splice search (the H3000 'deglitch' idea) remove most of the warble on single notes

presets.name: Early harmonizer thickener
presets.desc: Shifter 10 cents flat mixed 6 dB under the dry: the 1980s rack detune that fattens a rhythm guitar

refs.why: Eventide harmonizer detune mixed with the dry guitar

presets.notes: A tiny ratio makes the splices nearly inaudible; for a stereo ±cents pair, gfx-detune is the better tool

presets.name: Pitched-down snare
presets.desc: Snare or kit shifted down 5 semitones and blended with the dry: a deep, metallic, processed crack

refs.why: Visconti pitched the snare down through an H910 Harmonizer

presets.notes: Low uses H910 feedback for a falling pitch; this block has no feedback, so place a short delay after it for the descent

presets.name: Classic fifth harmony
presets.desc: A fixed fifth up with splice search, 4 dB under the dry: the old rack harmonizer on leads and synths

presets.name: Glitchy octave up
presets.desc: Octave up with short windows and hard splices, no search: a warbling, buzzing lo-fi octave
presets.notes: Short window and tiny overlap make every splice audible: here the artefact is the sound

presets.name: Splice stutter
presets.desc: A fourth up, fully wet, 100 ms windows with 1 ms crossfades: a choppy, stuttering repeat texture
presets.notes: Long windows repeat or skip whole fragments, and a 1 ms overlap clicks at each splice. Fully wet on purpose

detune.name: Detune
detune.help: 0 … ± 25 cents (to check against GxDetune's range in its source)

voices.name: Voices
voices.help: 2 = one up, one down (± detune), panned when stereo

presets.name: Stereo micro-shift
presets.desc: One voice 9 cents up left, one 9 cents down right, 12 ms late, under the dry: wide rhythm guitar

refs.why: Eventide harmonizer pair detuned a few cents each way, blended with the dry

presets.notes: detune × 25 ct: 0.36 = ±9 ct. The delay decorrelates the voices from the dry, so no chorus wobble; stereo lane needed

presets.name: Vocal micro-pitch widener
presets.desc: Voices ±7 cents, 18 ms late, under the lead vocal: a wider, thicker voice without a chorus wobble
presets.notes: The H3000 micro-pitch vocal trick: ±7 ct and 15–20 ms per side (Splice blog, 2016). 0.28 × 25 = 7 ct

presets.name: Subtle thickener
presets.desc: Voices ±5 cents with no offset, low in the mix: a barely-there thickening on any source
presets.notes: No delay: the 3 ms centre alone keeps it tight; for mono-safe width keep the wet low

presets.name: Big rack rhythm
presets.desc: Voices ±12 cents, 15 ms late, nearly as loud as the dry: the huge stereo rhythm of a 1980s rack rig

refs.why: wide, layered 1980s rhythm guitars

presets.notes: 0.5 = ±12.5 ct: obvious width, still in tune with the dry centred

presets.name: Mono doubletrack
presets.desc: One voice 4 cents up, 30 ms late: a mono artificial double-track for a voice or a guitar

refs.why: artificial double-tracking on lead vocals

presets.notes: One voice (up, on both sides): 30 ms is the longest offset, at the edge between a double and a slap

presets.name: Wide solo halo
presets.desc: Voices ±15 cents, 8 ms late, behind a lead: the solo spreads to both sides around a centred note

refs.why: harmonizer-widened lead tones

presets.name: Seasick out-of-tune
presets.desc: Voices ±25 cents, loud against the dry: a sour, honky-tonk, broken-tape detune
presets.notes: The full range: a quarter-tone spread each way reads as out of tune, on purpose

presets.name: Pad widener
presets.desc: Voices ±10 cents, 20 ms late, equal to the dry: synth pads and electric pianos spread wide

presets.name: Bass micro-thickener
presets.desc: Voices ±5 cents, no offset, low in the mix: bass gains growl and size without losing focus
presets.notes: Small and undelayed so the low end stays phase-coherent; the beating lives mostly in the upper harmonics

slot.name: Slot
slot.help: Identifies the probe in its messages

thresh.name: Silence Threshold
thresh.help: Envelope level under which the signal counts as silent

port.name: Port
port.help: UDP port; check-scene-gap.py binds it (never 9000, the bridge's REAPER feedback port, nor 3819, Ardour's surface)

tone.name: Test Tone
tone.help: Generator mode: output = tone, input discarded

presets.name: Gap probe, standard
presets.desc: Passes audio unchanged and reports every silence under -45 dB lasting 10 ms or more, on slot 0
presets.notes: The JSFX's values, which check-scene-gap.py expects; slot left at its default 0; set a distinct slot per probe

presets.name: Gap probe, micro-dropouts
presets.desc: Passes audio unchanged and reports silences under -60 dB as short as 2 ms: catches clicks and tiny dropouts
presets.notes: Only with the steady test tone upstream: on music, natural decays and rests would count as gaps

presets.name: Test tone generator
presets.desc: Replaces the input with a steady 196 Hz tone at -20 dB, so the probes downstream can measure scene-change gaps
presets.notes: 196 Hz is a guitar's open G; the input is discarded, so remove it after the measurement. level_db is meaningless here

thresh.name: Threshold
thresh.help: RMS level of the key under which the expansion starts (a sine reads 3 dB below its peak)

hold.name: Hold
hold.help: Keeps the gate open this long through short pauses before it fades

release.name: Release
release.help: Shortest fade from open to fully closed; 0 = the detector alone (the original Zuul)

ratio.name: Ratio
ratio.help: Expansion slope under the threshold: 2.8 = the Zuul; 10 ≈ a hard gate

smooth.name: Smoothing
smooth.help: Slow time constant of the detector; the fast one is 13 times shorter

adaptive.name: Adaptive
adaptive.help: The circuit's timing: a fall beyond 6.5 dB switches to the fast time constant

hpf.name: Key Low Cut
hpf.help: Extra high-pass on the key, on top of the fixed 32 Hz: ignores low-string thump

lpf.name: Key High Cut
lpf.help: Low-pass on the key: ignores pick noise and single-coil hiss

source.name: Detector Source
source.help: Key = the auxiliary input; Main until a key signal has been seen

listen.name: Listen
listen.help: Outputs the filtered key, for setting hpf and lpf

presets.name: Keyed expander, classic
presets.desc: 1:2.8 RMS expansion keyed from the DI with the circuit's slow-then-plunge fade: silent between chugs, attacks untouched

refs.why: their signature preamp builds in a keyed gate for staccato riffs

presets.notes: The original one-knob function: detector alone (hold and release 0). Key = lane DI so the threshold holds from clean to high gain

presets.name: Keyed expander, hold and fade
presets.desc: Classic keyed expansion plus 20 ms hold and a 60 ms fade: short pauses in staccato riffs stay open, then close clean

refs.why: staccato riffing that wants dead-silent stops between mutes
refs.source: Reverb.com, Misha Mansoor outlines the ultimate metal pedalboard (undated)

presets.notes: The doc's hold / release row, the two extra knobs of the plus version

presets.name: Hard gate for breakdowns
presets.desc: Near-switching 10:1 keyed expansion with a 30 ms fade: stop-start breakdowns cut to silence, still click-free
presets.notes: The doc's stop-start row; thresh a little higher than classic since the steep slope makes the knee obvious

presets.name: Surgical low-tuned chugs
presets.desc: 4:1 keyed expansion, faster detector and 100 Hz key low cut: eight-string chugs end on the beat, no thump reopen

refs.why: polyrhythmic chugs where every rest must be audible

presets.notes: Smoothing 40 ms (fast τ ≈ 3 ms) shortens the fall; key hpf keeps a low F# from holding the gate on its own thump

presets.name: Noisy pickups, low tuning
presets.desc: Classic keyed expansion with the key band-limited to 80 Hz – 5 kHz: low-string thump and pickup hiss do not open it
presets.notes: The doc's noisy-pickups row. Use listen to check the key band before lowering thresh

presets.name: Tremolo-picked thrash
presets.desc: Fast-detector keyed expansion that rides through tremolo picking and shuts within 20 ms of the stop
presets.notes: At 16th-note tremolo the RMS never falls between picks, so a short smoothing is safe and makes the stops crisp

presets.name: Ringing chords, gentle slope
presets.desc: 1:1.8 slope and slow 120 ms smoothing: sustained high-gain chords fade out naturally, hiss still goes
presets.notes: The doc's sustained-chords row with a little hold so let-ring arpeggios survive short gaps

presets.name: High-gain lead, open tails
presets.desc: Gentle 2:1 expansion with long hold and a 400 ms fade, floored at −40 dB: vibrato tails ring, hiss drops between phrases
presets.notes: Range −40 dB rather than silence: under delay and reverb a fully closed gate sounds like a mute

presets.name: Doom hiss floor
presets.desc: Mild 2:1 expansion floored at −25 dB with a slow fade: lowers fuzz hiss in rests without killing feedback swells
presets.notes: The floor keeps the room alive; slow smoothing means held, decaying chords never flutter at the threshold

presets.name: Expander on the lane, no key
presets.desc: Detects on its own input: a regular 2.2:1 expander with short hold and fade for rigs without a DI split
presets.notes: Place it before the amp when there is no key: post-amp, the noise floor follows the gain and the threshold must move with it

presets.name: Keyed metal bass
presets.desc: Keyed expansion for a distorted bass, slower 80 ms detector so low-B ripple never wobbles the gain
presets.notes: Key = bass DI. Low-pass on the key ignores fret clank; longer smoothing because a 31 Hz note's RMS ripples more

gain.name: Gain
gain.help: The drive pot (audio taper): clean mid boost at the bottom, a mid-range push above ~40 %

tone_stack.name: Tone
tone_stack.help: The 808 tone network: darkest at 0, the mid hump at half, presence above

level.name: Level
level.help: Output level; 0 dB = the hardware level pot fully up

headroom.name: Headroom
headroom.help: Clip knee relative to the MOSFET pair: −13 dB ≈ a Tube Screamer's diodes

asym.name: Asymmetry
asym.help: Lowers the negative knee (up to −50 %): an unmatched pair, even harmonics

tight.name: Tight
tight.help: Extra high-pass in the gain leg, on top of the 720 Hz; bypassed at 20 Hz

input.name: Input
input.help: Input trim, for a source hotter or weaker than a pickup at 0 dBFS = 1 V

bass_keep.name: Bass Keep
bass_keep.help: Below it: clean, so a bass keeps its fundamental

presets.name: Clean mid hump
presets.desc: Gain at zero: a clean +8 dB mid boost that tightens and focuses a high-gain amp
presets.notes: Fortin's 'Clean hump' setting. A boost, not a drive: the MOSFET knee is never reached, so keep it ON in high scenes

presets.name: Tighten up the gain
presets.desc: Gain low, tone a little under half: the classic Tube Screamer tightening, with more headroom
presets.notes: Fortin's 'Tighten up the gain' ('that classic TS thang'): still clean below the knee, so a boost for high scenes

presets.name: Drop-tuned tightener
presets.desc: Low-gain mid boost with an extra 120 Hz cut in the gain leg: keeps 7- and 8-string chugs defined

refs.why: a drive at low gain as a tight boost before high-gain amps

presets.notes: The README's main use, with tight 120 Hz for low tunings. The amp clips, the pedal barely does: keep it ON in high

presets.name: Metal lead boost
presets.desc: Mid boost with presence and a few dB of level: solos jump out of a high-gain rhythm tone
presets.notes: Gain 25 % still sits mostly under the high knee; it is a level-and-presence boost for the lead scene

presets.name: Front-end smash
presets.desc: Gain up, tone past half: a crushing mid-range push that drives an amp's front end hard
presets.notes: Fortin's 'Front end smash' (his level). It distorts by itself, so it is a drive: it turns a crunch amp into a heavy one and hits it far hotter than bypass

presets.name: Classic 808 overdrive
presets.desc: Tube Screamer knee and mid hump at half gain: smooth overdrive from a clean amp
presets.notes: headroom −13 dB puts the knee at a TS's silicon diodes: the 808 circuit, as it was

presets.name: 808 blues push
presets.desc: TS knee, low gain, level full: a mid push that makes a cranked clean amp break up and sing

refs.why: Tube Screamer with drive low and level high into cranked amps

presets.notes: Most of the drive comes from the amp; the pedal brings level and the mid hump

presets.name: Presence lead drive
presets.desc: Mid-high gain with the tone past three-quarters: a singing, present lead over a crunchy amp
presets.notes: The README's 'Lead with presence': the tone above half gives the highs back that the hump took

presets.name: Mid-push crunch
presets.desc: Moderate gain into a crunch amp: thicker, more saturated rhythm chords without losing the lows
presets.notes: The plugin default gain; level −6 dB keeps the scene from jumping when it engages

presets.name: Unmatched-pair grit
presets.desc: Asymmetric, lower knee: a gritty, even-harmonic overdrive into a clean amp
presets.notes: asym 50 % models a badly matched MOSFET pair, the 'irregular clipping' of the hardware

presets.name: Bass mid drive
presets.desc: 808-style drive on bass above 120 Hz, the fundamental kept clean: growl that keeps the bottom
presets.notes: The README's bass overdrive: bass_keep is phase-aligned, so no crossover ripple. Gain any: a bass drive stays on

presets.name: Driven organ
presets.desc: Input trimmed for line level, TS knee, warm tone: an organ or keys part pushed into overdrive

refs.why: Jon Lord's Hammond pushed through Marshall amps

presets.notes: Keys arrive hotter than a pickup: input −6 dB, and a lower knee so it still clips

grind.name: Grind
grind.help: The level pot: boost at the network's plateau

voice.name: Voice
voice.help: The shunt arm: Focused (2.7 kΩ) cuts more bass and boosts more; Full (11.8 kΩ) is ≈ 4.6 dB lower at the plateau

bright.name: Bright
bright.help: High shelf at 3 kHz, on top of the network

presets.name: Tight boost
presets.desc: Clean +10 dB boost through the fixed bass-cut / presence network: tight, defined high-gain rhythm

refs.why: Hagström's usual booster is a Fortin 33 in front of the amp

presets.notes: A boost with no clipping: the amp does all the distortion. Keep it ON in high scenes; lower the amp's gain

presets.name: Drop-tuning tight boost
presets.desc: +14 dB through the Focused network: low strings of 7- and 8-string guitars stay tight and clear

refs.why: 8-string polyrhythms that need a bass-tight boosted amp

presets.notes: More level through the same EQ: Fortin's upper travel, 'feels like there is more gain'. Boost class: high

presets.name: Pushed mids, less gain
presets.desc: Grind low: the network's bass cut and mid lift with almost no level, the amp barely pushed
presets.notes: Fortin's low travel: 'pushed mids feel, tight bass… almost feels like the gain has reduced'

presets.name: Scooped, tight, maximum push
presets.desc: Grind near the top: the most level into the amp, a scooped, aggressive feel with tight lows
presets.notes: Fortin's high travel: 'more scooped… feels like there is more gain'; the amp compresses harder

presets.name: Full-voice boost
presets.desc: The wider shunt arm: less bass cut and 4.6 dB less push, for standard tuning and fuller rhythms
presets.notes: Full keeps more lows than Focused; grind 12 lands near +7 dB at the plateau

presets.name: Tight boost, fizz tamed
presets.desc: The tight boost with the 3 kHz shelf down 3 dB: for amps that already sound bright or fizzy
presets.notes: The README's 'too fizzy amp': presence trimmed, the bass tightening kept

presets.name: Tight lead lift
presets.desc: More level and a touch of top on the same high-gain channel: the solo cuts without more mud
presets.notes: Same channel, more push: louder and more present, bass still cut

presets.name: Treble booster into crunch
presets.desc: Hard bass cut and a brighter top: a treble booster pushing a chiming, crunchy amp into lead

refs.why: Red Special into a Rangemaster treble booster into a Vox AC30
a treble booster sending his AC30 into thick overdrive

presets.notes: Not a Rangemaster circuit: the Focused network's steep bass cut plus bright +4 stands for it. The AC30 does the rest

presets.name: Crunch tightener
presets.desc: Moderate Full-voice boost into a crunch amp: punchier palm mutes for punk and hard rock
presets.notes: Into a crunch amp it tightens and adds a little saturation; no clipping of its own

presets.name: Bass high-lane push
presets.desc: Steep bass cut and push for the distorted lane of a split bass rig; the clean lane keeps the lows
presets.notes: Alone it thins a bass out: use it only on a lane that feeds a high-gain amp, with a parallel clean lane

shift.name: Interval
shift.help: Interval of the main double (−12 = one octave below)

formant.name: Formant
formant.help: The double's timbre: 0 = the voice's own, below = darker and bigger, above = lighter

voice1.name: Double Level
voice1.help: Level of the main double; 0 dB = as loud (RMS) as the dry voice; −6 dB = the *Emergence* preset

pan.name: Voice 2 Pan
pan.help: Equal-power position of voice 2 (voice 1 stays centred)

fine.name: Fine
fine.help: Detunes both doubles: with shift 0, a unison double

humanize.name: Humanize
humanize.help: Slow seeded drift of the doubles' pitch (±8 ct) and timing (±10 ms): a sung double rather than a coherent one

formant_link.name: Formant Follows Interval
formant_link.help: On: formants move with the interval; formant becomes an offset

glide.name: Glide
glide.help: Slows an interval change (scene), on top of the 1 st / ms slew

sens.name: Sensitivity
sens.help: Voicing thresholds: higher follows rougher notes

thresh.name: Threshold
thresh.help: Level gate: under it the doubles close (stage bleed between phrases)

register.name: Register
register.help: The voice's range; sets detection and the worst-case delay

hpf.name: Low Cut
hpf.help: High-pass on the doubles: an octave below a low male voice sits near 70 Hz, so the default stays under it

presets.name: Emergence
presets.desc: Phase-locked double one octave below the voice, own formants, 6 dB under the lead, centred

refs.why: an octave-below component follows the sung chorus line note for note, centred

presets.notes: The reference: formants kept so the double stays a voice; −6 dB is the listening-test setting of 2026-11-13. Put a de-esser and gate before it

presets.name: Emergence loud
presets.desc: The octave-below double as loud as the lead voice: a heavy, two-register chorus line

refs.why: the low octave carries the chorus as a full second register

presets.notes: 0 dB = double RMS equal to the dry: the chorus scene of a heavy song. Raise thresh on a loud stage (see emergence-stage)

presets.name: Emergence dark
presets.desc: Octave-below double with formants lowered 4 st: a bigger, darker, less human low voice

refs.why: the same octave double, voiced darker as the heavier option

presets.notes: Formant −4 moves the double's envelope down by 2^(−4/12): bigger throat, same pitch. The mix cannot tell whether the record did this; the ear decides

presets.name: Emergence dark loud
presets.desc: Dark octave-below double at the lead's level: an inhuman low voice for the heaviest chorus

refs.why: the octave double pushed darker and louder for a climax scene

presets.name: Whammy voice
presets.desc: Octave-below double whose formants follow the interval: the slowed-tape, pitched-down voice

refs.why: slowed, pitched-down voices where the timbre drops with the pitch

presets.notes: formant_link on: the envelope moves with the octave like a pitch pedal or a slowed tape, the opposite of the Emergence presets

presets.name: Choir
presets.desc: Octave below in the centre plus a softer octave above to one side, humanized: a three-register choir
presets.notes: Humanize 40 % makes the doubles drift like separate singers; a second instance with pan −60 mirrors it in stereo

presets.name: Unison double
presets.desc: Same-pitch double detuned 8 cents with slow pitch and timing drift: a double-tracked vocal live

refs.why: double-tracked lead vocals, the sound live doubling imitates

presets.notes: Humanize 60 % (±8 ct, ±10 ms drift) keeps the double from combing with the lead; fine 8 ct thickens without sounding out of tune

presets.name: Harmony third
presets.desc: A diatonic third above the voice in the song's key, 6 dB under the lead
presets.notes: In Scale mode shift 4 = a third in the scale. golem sets key / scale per song; C major is only the placeholder

presets.name: Octave double, loud stage
presets.desc: The Emergence octave double with a higher level gate and stricter voicing: no bleed doubled between lines
presets.notes: thresh −36 dB sits above typical wedge / backline bleed in the vocal mic; sens 35 % follows only clean sung notes, so screams and breaths stay single. Set thresh at soundcheck from state

presets.name: Baritone octave anchor
presets.desc: Octave-below double tracked in the Low register for baritone and bass singers, low cut at 30 Hz
presets.notes: A 100 Hz baritone note doubled an octave down sits near 50 Hz: Low register (60 Hz detection) and hpf 30 Hz keep it. Double delay rises to ≈ 19 ms worst case

presets.name: High-voice octave anchor
presets.desc: Octave-below double for soprano and head voice, High register: puts a chest-register line under it
presets.notes: High register (150 Hz – 1.2 kHz) tracks head voice without octave errors; formant −2 makes the double read as a second, lower singer

presets.name: Airy octave above
presets.desc: Quiet double one octave above, own formants, highs open: a breathy top line over a pop lead
presets.notes: Kept low (−14 dB) so it reads as air, not a second singer; formant 0 avoids the chipmunk timbre (see pitched-up-hook)

presets.name: Pitched-up hook double
presets.desc: Octave-above double with formants following the pitch: the sped-up, chipmunk vocal layer

refs.why: sped-up soul vocal samples, timbre raised with the pitch
pitched-up, formant-shifted vocal layers over the lead

presets.notes: formant_link on is what makes it sound sped-up rather than a second singer

presets.name: Pitched-down alter ego
presets.desc: A double a fourth below with lowered, linked formants, louder than the lead: a menacing second persona

refs.why: a pitched-down voice as a second character in the verses

presets.notes: voice1 +6 dB lets the shifted persona dominate (the dry cannot be muted); −5 st avoids the octave so it sounds like another voice, not a double

presets.name: Two-octave abyss
presets.desc: A double two octaves below, dark and band-limited: a sub-human drone under chanted or clean lines
presets.notes: −24 is PSOLA's hardest case (isolated grains, buzzy): low lpf hides it and −10 dB keeps it a shadow. Best on sustained notes

presets.name: Parallel fifth chant
presets.desc: A fifth below and an octave below, humanized: organum-like parallel chant from one voice
presets.notes: Fixed −7 / −12 (not Scale): parallel perfect intervals are the point of organum. Voice 2 centred

presets.name: Three-part in-key harmony
presets.desc: A diatonic third and fifth above in the song's key, spread left and centre: a stacked harmony choir

refs.why: real-time harmonies generated from Vernon's single voice
a harmonizer turning one voice into a chordal choir

presets.notes: Scale: shift 4 = a third, shift2 7 = a fifth above. The key is a placeholder golem replaces per song. Unlike those records, the intervals follow the scale, not a keyboard

presets.name: Close harmony below
presets.desc: A diatonic third under the melody, humanized: the duet harmony of folk and country choruses

refs.why: close harmony a third away from the melody

presets.notes: Scale: shift −3 = a third below. Humanize 45 % so the harmony breathes like a second singer. Key placeholder G major

presets.name: Wide stereo double
presets.desc: Two drifting unison doubles, one centred and one far to the side, detuned 10 cents: a wide pop lead
presets.notes: Needs a stereo lane; mirror with a second instance at pan −85 for symmetry. Humanize 70 % stops the comb a coherent unison would make

fx_a.name: Effect
fx_a.help: Slot A's effect: the pedal's main colour

amt_a.name: Amount
amt_a.help: How much of slot A's effect

sustain.name: Sustain
sustain.help: How long each partial rings after it is played (T60): the pad

mix.name: Mix
mix.help: Dry / wet: the dry stays at unity up to 50 %, then falls

size.name: Size
size.help: Analysis length: small = live and grainy, large = smooth pads and clouds; the wet is late by size + a quarter

window.name: Window
window.help: Frame shape: Raw splinters, Ringing buzzes at the frame rate

cloud.name: Cloud
cloud.help: Random phases each frame: from focused to a blurred wash

damp.name: Damp
damp.help: Shortens the sustain of the highs, like a real decaying pad

pitch.name: Pitch
pitch.help: Shifts the spectrum by semitones, partials kept whole

spread.name: Spread
spread.help: Stretches the partials apart (up) or squeezes them (down): inharmonic, bell-like

drift.name: Drift
drift.help: Moves every partial by the same Hz: metallic, detuned

lo_a.name: Region A Low
lo_a.help: Bottom of slot A's region, in octaves above 20 Hz

hi_a.name: Region A High
hi_a.help: Top of slot A's region, in octaves above 20 Hz

amt_b.name: Amount B
amt_b.help: How much of slot B's effect

amt_c.name: Amount C
amt_c.help: How much of slot C's effect

density.name: Density
density.help: Evens the bins out (fuller) or spreads them apart (sparser)

rate.name: LFO Rate
rate.help: The LFO's speed when not synced

sync.name: LFO Sync
sync.help: Locks the LFO to the host tempo

lfo_depth.name: LFO Depth
lfo_depth.help: How far the LFO moves its destination

env_sens.name: Envelope Sensitivity
env_sens.help: How soft a pick still opens the envelope

env_att.name: Envelope Attack
env_att.help: How fast the envelope follows the pick

env_depth.name: Envelope Depth
env_depth.help: How far the envelope moves its destination; negative ducks

width.name: Width
width.help: How differently the two channels' randoms move

align.name: Align Dry
align.help: Delays the dry to match the wet; setup only, never a scene value

trails.name: Trails
trails.help: The wet rings out when the pedal is bypassed

presets.name: Ringing partials
presets.desc: The strong partials of each chord ring on for seconds while the weak ones die: a halo that follows the playing
presets.notes: Ring Hold keeps what the guitar puts forward; sustain 1.5 s glues the chord changes without smearing them

presets.name: Chord into pad
presets.desc: Each strum stacks into a steady pad that decays over six seconds; play single notes over it

refs.why: in the spirit of: chords swelling into long guitar pads

presets.notes: 4,096 points smooth the pad; damp 40 % lets the top fade first, density +30 % evens the chord out

presets.name: Cloud wash
presets.desc: A long analysis with random phases: everything played turns into a slowly evolving, blurred wash

refs.why: in the spirit of: guitar dissolved into slow drones

presets.notes: The wet arrives ~0.4 s late at this size: a wash, not an echo. Cloud 80 % removes every transient

presets.name: Slow swell
presets.desc: Notes swell and hang like a bowed string, evened out by the per-bin compander
presets.notes: No slot: sustain and density alone. The 8,192-point frame softens every attack

presets.name: Octave organ
presets.desc: Sustained chords doubled an octave up, rolled off: an organ-like layer under the dry guitar
presets.notes: Pitch acts on the sustained spectrum, so the octave rings as long as the pad

presets.name: Sub-octave drone
presets.desc: The pad an octave down, dark and long: a bed under clean arpeggios
presets.notes: Low cut at 40 Hz keeps the drone's fundamental and drops rumble below

presets.name: Shimmering haze
presets.desc: Only the top of the spectrum (2.5 – 12 kHz) held and sparkling: air above the dry guitar
presets.notes: Both slots on 7 – 9.3 octaves above 20 Hz; the body of the guitar stays dry

presets.name: Lo-fi arpeggio
presets.desc: Bin levels and phases quantised like a low-bitrate codec on clean picking
presets.notes: 1,024 points keep it live (27 ms); mix 100 % because a coherent wet beside the dry would comb

presets.name: Broken codec
presets.desc: A corrupted decoder with shuffled bins: chirps, dropouts and metallic smears
presets.notes: Corrupt reads the level table off by a few steps; Shuffle swaps bins every 20 ms

presets.name: Stereo stutter
presets.desc: The spectrum freezes in short random bursts, on the sixteenth, differently left and right
presets.notes: Width 100 % gives each channel its own random holds; the LFO steps the amount on the grid

presets.name: Attack freeze
presets.desc: Each pick attack freezes its own spectrum for a moment: notes leave short frozen ghosts
presets.notes: Holds from 0.2 to 0.7 s at 60 %; harder picking triggers more often

presets.name: Metal bells
presets.desc: Every partial moved up by 150 Hz and thinned: chords turn into bells and struck metal
presets.notes: Drift shifts by Hz, not by ratio, so the harmonics stop being harmonic

presets.name: Ghost partials
presets.desc: Only the loudest peaks survive and linger: a sparse, ghostly echo of the chord
presets.notes: Quiet Cut removes everything 27 dB under the peak; Peak Only thins what is left

presets.name: Breathing band
presets.desc: A narrow band of the guitar (400 Hz – 2 kHz) that slowly drifts up and down the spectrum
presets.notes: The LFO moves both edges of region A by up to 2 octaves; mix 100 % to avoid a comb with the dry

presets.name: Scattered sparks
presets.desc: Random high bins freeze for a moment and scatter across the stereo field above the chords
presets.notes: Scatter Hold above 1.3 kHz; a little cloud keeps the held bins from sounding like a tone

presets.name: Stretched chords
presets.desc: Partials stretched apart, as on a bell or a prepared piano: chords sound inharmonic and wide
presets.notes: Spread +60 % raises each partial's frequency to the power 1.15 around 100 Hz

presets.name: Ducking pad
presets.desc: A long pad that dips while you play and blooms back in the gaps between phrases
presets.notes: The envelope pulls the wet down by up to 70 % while you pick; the 600 ms release lets the pad return smoothly
