presets.name: Standard
presets.desc: Every fader at 0 dB: bit-transparent, the starting point to draw a curve from
presets.notes: golem's Standard preset kept as is

presets.name: Bass smiley
presets.desc: +4 dB at 60 Hz and +2 at 2 – 4 kHz around a small 500 Hz dip, the top rolled off: a round, present bass
presets.notes: golem's preset kept as is; its top two faders now act at 12 and 16 kHz (GxGraphicEQ's top bands sat higher)

presets.name: Hygiaphone
presets.desc: Everything below 250 Hz and above 8 kHz at -12 dB, a +4 dB bump at 1 – 2 kHz: a voice through a ticket-window grille
presets.notes: golem's preset kept as is. The faders hold their values: -12 at 8 kHz is -12 there, not a gentle skirt

presets.name: Lead boost
presets.desc: +3 dB at 1 kHz and +4 at 2 kHz, the 8 kHz fizz down 1 dB: a lead that cuts through without more gain
presets.notes: golem's preset kept as is

presets.name: Lo-fi radio
presets.desc: Lows and highs falling away from a +3 dB 500 Hz – 1 kHz hump: a small transistor radio
presets.notes: golem's preset kept as is; the top cut starts at 12 kHz here, a little lower and more audible than on GxGraphicEQ

presets.name: Vocal shape
presets.desc: Lows below 125 Hz cut hard, +2 – 3 dB from 4 to 12 kHz: a clear, airy voice above the band
presets.notes: golem's preset kept as is

presets.name: V shape
presets.desc: -4 dB at 1 kHz and -3 at 500 Hz between a +2 dB 125 Hz and +3 at 4 kHz: a scooped rhythm
presets.notes: golem's preset kept as is

presets.name: Solo lift
presets.desc: Guitar 7: +4 dB at 800 Hz, +3 at 1.6 kHz, +1 at 400 Hz and 3 dB of level: the solo voicing on a footswitch
presets.notes: The classic 7-band trick: a mid lift plus level. Accurate mode means +4 at 800 Hz is +4, with no pile-up between 800 and 1.6k

presets.name: Mid push for fuzz
presets.desc: Guitar 7: +2 dB at 400 Hz, +5 at 800 Hz, +3 at 1.6 kHz: puts back the mids a fuzz scoops out
presets.notes: After a scooped fuzz, so it is heard in a band mix instead of disappearing under the bass and cymbals

presets.name: Tight front end
presets.desc: -15 dB at 30 Hz, -10 at 60 Hz, -4 at 125 Hz, +3 at 1 kHz and +2 at 2 kHz: a tight low end into a high-gain amp
presets.notes: Before the amp: the lows the amp would turn into mush are cut by faders, with no peaking at 125 Hz

presets.name: Scooped rhythm
presets.desc: After the amp: +2 dB at 250 Hz and 8 kHz around -4 to -5 dB at 500 Hz – 1 kHz
presets.notes: Post-amp scoop; for a band mix keep it shallow, the mids are where a guitar is heard

presets.name: Post-cab tame
presets.desc: Low cut 80 Hz, steep high cut 8 kHz and -2 dB at 4 kHz: a cab sim's rumble and fizz removed
presets.notes: The cuts the faders cannot do: a 30 Hz fader at -15 dB is not a high-pass

presets.name: Slap smile
presets.desc: Bass 7: +4 dB at 50 Hz and 10 kHz, +3 at 4.5 kHz, -4 / -3 dB at 400 / 500 Hz: a slap bass scoop
presets.notes: The two low-mid faders a third of an octave apart make one clean dip, with no hole between them

presets.name: Bass growl
presets.desc: Bass 7: +5 dB at 800 Hz, +2 at 120 Hz, -2 at 4.5 kHz: a growling, midrange-forward bass
presets.notes: The 800 Hz push is what lets a bass be heard on small speakers and under distorted guitars

presets.name: Piezo de-quack
presets.desc: Low cut 70 Hz, -4 dB at 1 kHz and -2 at 500 Hz, +2 at 12 kHz: an acoustic's piezo without the quack
presets.notes: The piezo's honk lives around 1 kHz; the 12 kHz lift gives back some of the air a mic would hear

presets.name: Telephone
presets.desc: Low cut 300 Hz, steep high cut 3.4 kHz and +4 dB at 1 kHz: a telephone line
presets.notes: The telephone band is 300 Hz – 3.4 kHz; the cuts do it, the 1 kHz fader adds the honk

presets.name: Bright clean sparkle
presets.desc: +3 dB at 8 kHz, +2 at 12 kHz and -2 at 125 Hz: a clean guitar with more sheen and less boom

presets.name: Dark jazz
presets.desc: -4 dB at 4 kHz down to -8 at 12 kHz, +2 at 125 Hz: a dark, round archtop tone

presets.name: Bedroom to stage
presets.desc: -3 dB at 60 Hz and +2 at 2 kHz: a tone dialled at home that would boom and vanish in a room with a band

shift.name: Shift L
shift.help: Moves every partial by this many Hz (left, and the base of the right)

fbk.name: Feedback
fbk.help: The shifted wet fed back: each pass is shifted again

time.name: Time
time.help: Delay before the shifter, inside the loop

mix.name: Mix
mix.help: Linear dry / wet crossfade (the catalogue's law)

shift_r.name: Shift R
shift_r.help: Right shift as a ratio of the left: +100 % = same (phase-locked), 0 = right unshifted, −100 % = opposite (stereo spread)

loop.name: Loop
loop.help: Phaser adds a dispersive 12-stage all-pass chain in the loop: a denser barber-pole phaser at time 0 (Delay alone already phases, through the Hilbert pair)

sideband.name: Sideband
sideband.help: +100 = the signed shift only; 0 = both sidebands (carrier-free ring mod); −100 = the mirror (Bode's Up / Down mix)

zero_cut.name: Zero Cut
zero_cut.help: Removes the partials shifted below 0 Hz (no mud) or past Nyquist, by a second pass through the Hilbert pair

dry_match.name: Dry Match
dry_match.help: Dry through the wet's own all-pass path: small shifts swell like a tremolo instead of phasing; shift 0 nulls to −83 dB

time_sync.name: Time Sync
time_sync.help: time from the host tempo (a duration)

low_cut.name: Loop Low Cut
low_cut.help: In the feedback return: each pass thinner

high_cut.name: Loop High Cut
high_cut.help: In the feedback return: each pass darker; tames upward spirals

lfo_depth.name: LFO Depth
lfo_depth.help: ± Hz added to the shift by the LFO; may cross zero

sync.name: LFO Sync
sync.help: LFO period and phase from the host position (shared id)

env_depth.name: Envelope Depth
env_depth.help: Hz added by the input envelope: the pick pushes the shift

presets.name: Endless phase
presets.desc: Every partial moved up 0.3 Hz against the dry: notches that climb for ever and never turn round
presets.notes: The barber-pole phaser with no feedback: the dry beats against the shifted wet; 50 % mix gives the deepest notches

presets.name: Spiral phaser
presets.desc: A dense barber-pole phaser: the shifted wet fed back through a twelve-stage all-pass chain
presets.notes: Costello's recipe: a dispersive loop around the shifter; more feedback, sharper notches

presets.name: Falling flanger
presets.desc: Comb teeth that glide down for ever: a 3 ms loop shifted −0.4 Hz on every pass
presets.notes: A short delay in the loop turns the barber-pole phaser into a flanger; the loop high cut keeps the teeth smooth

presets.name: Wide metallic detune
presets.desc: Left shifted up 1.5 Hz, right down 1.5 Hz, 12 ms late: a sweet metallic chorus that spreads wide
presets.notes: Opposite stereo shifts; summed to mono they are both sidebands, a slow ring-mod shimmer

presets.name: Whole-band swell
presets.desc: The whole chord swells and fades four times a second: the dry matched to the wet's phase
presets.notes: Dry Match puts every partial's beat in phase: a tremolo made of beating, not a phaser

presets.name: Bell lead
presets.desc: Every partial moved up 180 Hz: harmonics turn inharmonic, single notes ring like bells
presets.notes: Inharmonic partials over a dry core; play single notes, chords turn to clang

presets.name: Carrier-free ring mod
presets.desc: Both sidebands at ±400 Hz, no carrier and no dry: a clean ring modulator
presets.notes: Sideband 0 mixes the shift and its mirror at −6 dB each: a sine ring modulator without carrier bleed

presets.name: Through-zero swirl
presets.desc: The shift swings ±3 Hz around zero: the phasing slows, stops and reverses on a slow cycle
presets.notes: The oscillator's phase is continuous, so crossing 0 Hz never steps

presets.name: Pick zap
presets.desc: Each pick attack pushes the shift up to 600 Hz and lets it fall back: a zap on every note
presets.notes: The envelope drives the shift in Hz; play staccato for separate zaps

presets.name: Falling ghost echoes
presets.desc: Echoes 350 ms apart, each one 30 Hz lower and thinner than the last
presets.notes: Zero Cut keeps the falling repeats from folding back into mud below 0 Hz

presets.name: Rising spiral echoes
presets.desc: Quarter-second echoes that climb 12 Hz per repeat and darken as they go
presets.notes: A shifter in a delay loop; Zero Cut also removes what climbs past Nyquist

presets.name: Runaway wall
presets.desc: Feedback past 100 %: the loop builds into a bounded, ever-rising wall; lower it to recover
presets.notes: Meant for an EXP pedal on Feedback; the soft clip on the return keeps it bounded

presets.name: Bass growl
presets.desc: Bass shifted 60 Hz down with the zero cut off: low notes fold back through 0 Hz and growl
presets.notes: The through-zero reflection on purpose; mixed low so the fundamental stays

presets.name: Radio ghost
presets.desc: A 24 Hz shift with a short, faint loop and a nearly dry right side: a voice between stations
presets.notes: The catalogue's radio-ghost converted to real units (README §3.4)

presets.name: Metal smear
presets.desc: Partials moved up 40 Hz on the left, 16 Hz on the right, smeared by a 15 ms loop
presets.notes: The catalogue's metal-smear converted to real units (README §3.4)

presets.name: Barber pole
presets.desc: A 4 Hz shift in a 144 ms loop: echoes that each beat faster, a slow spinning pole
presets.notes: The catalogue's barberpole in real units, with Shift R at +100 % (R = L) as its author meant

rise.name: Rise
rise.help: Swell time from start to full level (when sync = Off)

sync.name: Sync
sync.help: Rise as a note value at the host tempo

sens.name: Sensitivity
sens.help: Pick threshold (rise 12 → 3 dB) and the window below the playing level that may trigger (18 → 48 dB)

legato.name: Legato
legato.help: Sensitivity of the pickless detectors (shape flux, pitch jump); 0 = picks only (and cheaper)

depth.name: Depth
depth.help: How far below unity a swell starts: 100 % = from silence, 50 % = attack softened by 6 dB

dip.name: Retrigger Dip
dip.help: How far a new note pulls a ringing note down before swelling; 0 = swell only after silence

strum.name: Strum Window
strum.help: Onsets this close to the first one merge into one swell (strums, slides); also the fastest retrigger

decay.name: Decay (Bow)
decay.help: After the rise, fall back to the start level: attack-decay bows, reverse-tape

reset.name: Reset
reset.help: The swell resets (gain back to the start) once the note has decayed this far below its body level; falling under thresh always resets

release.name: Reset Fade
release.help: Fade to the start level on reset

thresh.name: Noise Floor
thresh.help: Absolute floor: nothing below it triggers or holds a note (hiss, hum)

source.name: Detector Source
source.help: Key = the auxiliary input (the clean DI when the swell sits after the amp)

lookahead.name: Lookahead
lookahead.help: Delays the audio, reported to the host: perfect removal of retriggered attacks

fire.name: Fire
fire.help: Each off → on edge starts a swell (footswitch)

bypass.name: Bypass
bypass.help: The VST3 bypass parameter (make_bypass): golem switches the block with it, so engaging is seen

presets.name: Violin
presets.desc: Each picked note fades in from silence over a quarter second; stop each note before the next
presets.notes: Stopping each note lets the swell reset, so the next pick meets a closed gain: the attack is removed at zero latency

presets.name: Violin after the amp
presets.desc: The violin swell placed after the drive or amp, listening to the clean DI on the key input
presets.notes: Detection on the clean DI: a distorted signal has few transients left and lifts the hiss; needs the DI routed to the key bus

presets.name: Cello pad
presets.desc: Strummed chords swell in slowly as one bowed pad, one swell per strum; best into a long reverb
presets.notes: An 80 ms strum window merges slow strums into one swell; the S-curve lands softly

presets.name: Legato lead
presets.desc: Hammer-ons, pull-offs and slides swell too, not only picked notes; a slide swells once
presets.notes: The pitch-jump detector answers 8 – 16 ms after a legato note: a short blip, then the swell; lookahead 25 ms removes it in the studio

presets.name: Gentle bow changes
presets.desc: A new note only pulls the ringing one down a little before swelling: smooth bow changes
presets.notes: Dip 35 % keeps two thirds of the ringing note under the new one

presets.name: Reverse tape
presets.desc: Every note rises over a quarter note and stops dead: a backwards-tape feel locked to the tempo
presets.notes: Long rise, 40 ms decay: the attack-decay bow of the reverse-tape pedals

presets.name: Bowed stabs
presets.desc: Each note swells in fast and fades away by itself: a bowed attack and decay per note
presets.notes: With a decay the swell is spent after each bow; only a new pick, legato note or fire starts another

presets.name: Tempo swells
presets.desc: Swells that take a half note at the song's tempo, with a pedal-like taper; feed a dotted delay and a long reverb
presets.notes: The swell starts at the note, not on the grid; only its length follows the tempo

presets.name: Soft attack
presets.desc: Takes the edge off each pick: a 25 ms linear fade from half level, nothing else changes
presets.notes: Depth 50 % starts each note 6 dB down: a transient softener rather than a swell

presets.name: Foot swell
presets.desc: Swells only when the footswitch fires: re-swell a held chord on demand
presets.notes: Map Fire to a momentary footswitch; sens 0 and legato 0 leave the picks and legato detectors at their least eager

presets.name: Live clean retriggers
presets.desc: The violin swell with 3 ms of lookahead: re-picked notes lose their attack completely
presets.notes: 3 ms of reported latency hides every pick's dip; set at insert, never switched inside a song

presets.name: Studio perfect swell
presets.desc: The violin swell with 25 ms of lookahead: picked and legato notes all start at silence
presets.notes: For recording and re-amping: 25 ms of reported latency places the legato dips too, down to about 145 Hz

presets.name: Bowed bass
presets.desc: Bass notes fade in like a bowed double bass, at any playing level
presets.notes: Pitch jumps are read above 75 Hz only (from the D string's first frets up); below, legato swells through the flux detector or not at all

presets.name: Pads and keys
presets.desc: Removes the attack of keys and pads: each new chord swells in, even without a transient
presets.notes: The level gate opens after each silence; the flux detector catches a new chord over a ringing one

quant.name: Quant
quant.help: Word size of the virtual converter; fractional for Linear (a sweep has no steps)

rate.name: Rate
rate.help: The virtual clock; 48,000 (or R ≥ fs) = Off

nonlin.name: Non-Lin
nonlin.help: The DAC's power-law curve (thickening), level-neutral at −18 dBFS

law.name: Format
law.help: Word format: uniform, companded or gain-ranging words

quantizer.name: Quantizer
quantizer.help: Where zero sits: silence stays silent / buzzes / dead zone (MDA)

dither.name: Dither
dither.help: TPDF, 100 % = ±1 LSB; tails fade it too

tails.name: Tails
tails.help: Below 1 – 2 LSB: unquantised tail / silence / as is

input.name: Input
input.help: Drive into the converter (clip, use of bits); output compensated

asym.name: Asymmetry
asym.help: Share of nonlin applied to one polarity only (even harmonics)

ladder.name: DAC Error
ladder.help: R-2R bit-weight mismatch: grit on quiet signals (Linear, Float)

rate_shift.name: Rate Shift
rate_shift.help: Transposes the clock down (R = rate · 2^(st / 12)): the EXP sweep control, pitch-like feel

jitter.name: Jitter
jitter.help: Clock jitter, ±25 % of a period at 100 % (seeded)

track.name: Track
track.help: Rate locked to N × the played pitch: aliases on the harmonic series (best at R ≤ 8 kHz)

sync.name: Sync
sync.help: Locks the rate LFO to the host tempo (Off: Mod Rate sets it)

env_sens.name: Envelope Sensitivity
env_sens.help: How strongly the playing level drives the rate modulation

env_att.name: Envelope Attack
env_att.help: How fast the envelope follows a rising level

env_rel.name: Envelope Release
env_rel.help: How fast the envelope falls back after a note

presets.name: 8-bit lead
presets.desc: Classic crush: 8-bit words at 16 kHz, aliasing kept, quiet tails faded to clean instead of fizzing
presets.notes: The default: heard at once on insert. Tails Clean keeps a gain stage after it from turning the sputter into fizz

presets.name: Rack sampler 12-bit
presets.desc: Warm 12-bit grit at 26 kHz through steep anti-alias and reconstruction filters
presets.notes: The rack sampler's warmth is its filters, not its bits: 6th-order Butterworth either side of the converter

presets.name: Sampled guitar 12-bit
presets.desc: Clean guitar through a 12-bit sampler at 26 kHz: softened top, grainy tails
presets.notes: Rack Sampler 12 for a clean guitar part played as if sampled from a record

presets.name: Hot-sampled 26k
presets.desc: Drum-machine 12-bit at 26 kHz, sampled with no input filter: ringing aliases, softened images
presets.notes: Aliasing kept on purpose, a 4-pole ladder on the output: the drum-machine voicing [to tune by ear]

presets.name: Companded 8-bit
presets.desc: µ-law 8-bit words at 28 kHz: grain on loud notes, clean quiet tails, no fizz
presets.notes: Eight bits through a µ-law DAC: about 12 bits of dynamic range, the 80s drum machines' trick

presets.name: Phone line
presets.desc: Telephone voice: µ-law 8-bit at 8 kHz, band-limited 300 – 3,400 Hz
presets.notes: G.711's word and band; Clean decimation so nothing folds back into the voice

presets.name: AM radio
presets.desc: Narrow, slightly thickened voice: µ-law 8-bit at 11 kHz, 300 – 4,500 Hz
presets.notes: The old catalogue "AM radio" by intent: band-limited, a touch of DAC curve for density

presets.name: 1-bit fuzz
presets.desc: A one-bit square of the input, gated cleanly as the note decays
presets.notes: Riser at 1 bit is a square whatever the level; input +24 dB sets where the gate closes (about −18 dBFS of DI)

presets.name: Tuned crush
presets.desc: Rate locked to a multiple of the played note: the aliases land on its harmonics, in tune
presets.notes: Monophonic lines: chords hold the last rate. Best at R ≤ 8 kHz where the pitch error beats slowly

presets.name: Tuned arpeggio
presets.desc: Pitch-locked crush stepped through harmonic multiples by an eighth-note LFO
presets.notes: The LFO moves the target rate; track rounds it to whole multiples of f0: an arpeggio of crushes

presets.name: Sample-rate sweep
presets.desc: Expression-pedal sweep of the clock from 48 kHz down to 750 Hz: a glide, no zipper
presets.notes: Assign EXP to rate_shift (0 → −72 st): pitch-like travel, the fractional clock glides between every rate

presets.name: Pick-harder crush
presets.desc: The rate drops as the attack rises: harder picking crunches more
presets.notes: Envelope on the clock, negative depth: dynamics play the crush

presets.name: Synced wobble
presets.desc: Clock swept by an eighth-note sine around 8 kHz, locked to the tempo
presets.notes: Deterministic and host-synced: the same wobble on every take

presets.name: Dusty jitter
presets.desc: 10-bit sampler at 12 kHz with a wandering clock: aliases smeared into dust
presets.notes: Clock jitter turns the images and aliases into noise while the pitch stays put

presets.name: Parallel grit
presets.desc: Six-bit crush at 6 kHz blended under the dry: grit on top, the low end kept
presets.notes: The dry runs through the kernels' own response: no comb in the blend below the rate

presets.name: Old ladder DAC
presets.desc: 12-bit sampler whose ladder DAC mis-steps at mid-scale: crossover grit on quiet notes
presets.notes: R-2R bit-weight errors: quiet signals cross the wrong-sized mid-scale step [magnitude to tune by ear]

presets.name: Hit the converter
presets.desc: Input pushed 12 dB into a 10-bit converter: hard digital clipping, level compensated
presets.notes: Rate Off: the clip runs at the host rate, as a real overloaded ADC

presets.name: Clean decimate
presets.desc: Bandwidth only: 16-bit at 8 kHz through elliptic filters, no foldover
presets.notes: A brick-wall "small speaker": the Clean model removes every alias
